data.title: Healthy soil is the hidden ingredient
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了欧洲土壤健康问题，尤其是西班牙的土壤退化状况。欧盟60-70%的土壤处于不健康状态，导致每年约€500亿的损失。西班牙是土壤侵蚀最严重的国家，每年每公顷流失约14.2吨土壤。地理学家Jesús Rodrigo Comino通过地理绘图系统和人工智能研究葡萄园的土壤侵蚀，致力于开发可持续的土壤管理实践，帮助农民做出决策，如灌溉和种植覆盖作物。他还参与了欧盟的SOILCRATES项目，旨在通过实验提高人们对土壤健康的认识。气候变化对土壤健康的影响日益显著，如气温升高和极端降雨事件增加。尽管有些农民开始采用良好实践，但仍需更多努力改善土壤质量。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：土壤健康与改良方法及其相关技术应用

不同观点：
• [econ] 和 [pdfernhout] 提到古代文明可能已经深入研究过土壤改良（如Terra Preta），并提出现代方法如岩石粉末（rock dust）可以有效恢复土壤肥力。他们强调了长期研究和历史经验在土壤管理中的价值。
• [bgnn] 分享了个人园艺经验，强调了通过堆肥、无挖耕作等方式改良土壤的过程，并指出与微生物互动和自然实验的重要性。尽管过程复杂且存在失败，但通过持续努力可以获得成功。
• [contingencies] 也分享了在贫瘠土壤上种植的经验，通过改变植物种类、覆盖物和有机废物等方式逐步改善土壤质量。重点在于耐心地通过多种方法结合来改善不同类型的土壤。
• [ralusek] 对土壤健康的神秘化提出质疑，认为植物基本需求只是水、光和肥料，并指出通过合成肥料和土壤添加剂也可以实现植物健康生长。不过，他也承认培养良好的土壤可以实现自我维持，减少额外输入。

补充讨论：
• [tbrownaw] 和 [zeristor] 提到了使用人工智能（AI）和地理信息系统（GIS）等技术来评估和改善土壤质量，表明科技在土壤管理中的潜在应用。
• [jimbobthemighty] 分享了一篇关于植物“垃圾食品”问题的文章，强调不良土壤管理可能导致的问题。
• [photochemsyn] 提出了重金属污染对土壤健康的威胁，强调了工业和矿业历史对农业土壤的潜在风险，并引用了相关文献支持其观点。
• [bethekidyouwant] 质疑了关于健康土壤的浪漫化描述，指出大规模农业生产中依赖人工劳动改良土壤的不现实性。
• [poorna12] 提到了Sadhguru通过骑行活动传播保护土壤的信息，强调了公众意识在土壤保护中的重要性。
• [SwayamDas] 总结了改良土壤所需的主要成分，包括有机物、微生物、土壤动物、养分、土壤结构和水管理，提供了一个综合的土壤改良框架。

争议焦点：
• 关于是否需要依赖合成肥料和土壤添加剂来实现植物健康生长存在争议。
• 有人质疑土壤健康管理中的神秘化和浪漫化描述，认为科技和合成方法也能有效改良土壤。
• 重金属污染问题在土壤健康讨论中被提出，但其实际监测和标准执行存在争议。

总结：评论主要围绕土壤改良方法、个人经验分享、科技应用及相关争议展开，涉及历史经验、现代科技、合成与自然方法的比较以及重金属污染等多个方面。

Soil quality is crucial for sustaining production in vineyards, such as this one near Montilla in southern Spain.
Credit: JORGE GUERRERO/AFP via Getty
When it comes to the land, the European Union faces a reckoning: 60–70% of its soils are considered unhealthy, resulting in soil degradation. That costs €50 billion (US$55 billion) annually because of the loss of essential services and the effect on human health. Spain has the highest rates of soil degradation in Europe, with an average of 14.2 tonnes of soil lost per hectare to erosion each year
1
. Although its importance is often overlooked, quality soil is essential for sustaining agriculture and crucial ecosystems. Its importance was highlighted in the 2015 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, with soil health named as a key factor in achieving several of the goals.
Nature Spotlight: Spain
Having studied soil erosion in vineyards across Europe, Jesús Rodrigo Comino, a geographer at the University of Granada, Spain, is hoping to unearth a solution. Now he works with farmers, researchers and policymakers to test and use more-sustainable soil-management practices in vineyards and more broadly. Rodrigo Comino speaks to
Nature
about his research programme and why healthy soils are important for Spain’s cultural heritage and economy.
Tell us about your work in soil science.
I was always a curious kid, but my passion for soil science began with my studies at the University of Malaga in Spain and at Trier University in Germany. My home region of Andalusia in Spain has some really beautiful landscapes, but some areas are heavily degraded because of soil erosion and other factors. I felt compelled to find solutions to these problems.
When I came back to Spain in 2021 after doing my PhD and a postdoctoral position in Germany, I started a project to assess soil erosion and degradation in vineyards using geographical mapping systems and artificial intelligence (AI). Soil erosion is caused by natural factors, such as extreme rainfall events and strong winds, as well as by human-driven activities, including tillage and urbanization. AI helps me to design and polish the software codes that I use to create geographical maps and analyse data. The main idea is to develop tools to help farmers make decisions. These might be about how to apply irrigation systems; which types of cover crop to plant; or when to till the soil, if necessary, to prevent soil degradation.
Geographer Jesús Rodrigo Comino examines the soil at a vineyard.
Credit: Jesús Rodrigo Comino
I’m also involved in a Soil Living Labs project called SOILCRATES, which is part of an EU mission called A Soil Deal for Europe. The goal is to create field sites where soil scientists, agronomists, stakeholders and policymakers come together to conduct experiments and establish plots with sustainable soils. As part of the project, we also aim to show people how important fertile soils are to their lives and how their actions can affect soil health. The EU is now investing in a variety of projects to improve soil quality and enhance people’s understanding of soil. I’ve seen people implementing good practices to reduce soil erosion. But we’re not there yet — much more work is needed.
How has climate change affected your work?
It is evident that many places, especially urban ones, are experiencing an increase in temperature and a reduction in precipitation volume. We’re also seeing a concentration of extreme rainfall events in short periods of time, such as the flooding that happened in Valencia in Spain last year. All of these factors can affect soil health.
When it comes to the vineyards in Spain, we don’t yet have enough data to confirm whether and how climate change is altering them — but the trends are clear. We know that vineyards are encountering higher temperatures now than they did in the past, and that this is causing the vines to flower earlier. Annual rainfall is being concentrated into shorter time periods, and we’re also experiencing extreme rainfall events, which cause soil erosion.
What are farmers telling you about their experiences?

data.title: Crows can recognize geometric regularity
data.author: wglb
data.article_summary: 德国图宾根大学的研究人员发现，乌鸦能够识别几何规律。在发表于《Science Advances》期刊的研究中，Philipp Schmidbauer、Madita Hahn和Andreas Nieder通过实验测试了乌鸦识别几何形状的能力。实验中，乌鸦需要从一组刺激物中啄出不同的形状，选对可获得食物奖励。实验显示，乌鸦能识别出如星星与月亮、非对称四边形与对称四边形等不同形状。即使面对细微差异，乌鸦的准确率也高于随机选择。研究表明，乌鸦具备一定的几何规律识别能力，且无需事先学习。这一发现暗示其他动物也可能具备类似能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：动物的智力及其与人类智力的比较

不同观点：
• CountWSS认为，认为“只有人类能够识别形状”这一观点已经过时，类似于“科学证实动物会感到疼痛”的发现。这表明动物的智力可能被低估。
• Terretta引用Adrian Tchaikovsky的小说《Children of Memory》中的乌鸦智能为例，探讨“什么是智力”的问题，并通过熟悉的例子来定义可能过于陌生的概念。
• Sayamqazi分享个人经历，表示山羊能够通过嘴巴旋转门栓手柄并打开门，说明动物的问题解决能力常被低估。
• Djmips描述观察到乌鸦在水中软化人类丢弃的食物以便食用，显示乌鸦的创造性行为。

补充讨论：
• Worldsayshi提问乌鸦、海豚、章鱼和非人类猿类的智力如何比较，是否存在巨大的智力差距，以及这种差距是否可以量化。
• Almosthere简单指出乌鸦可以从300英尺外识别出虫子，表明其识别能力。
• SwtCyber提到乌鸦在视觉任务中的表现下降但仍高于随机选择，表明它们可能在“思考”而不仅仅是反应。
• Wglb提供了一篇Science Advances论文链接，为讨论提供科学依据。
• Cdplayer96幽默地询问训练乌鸦收集城市中散落的硬币是否合法。
• Alexfromapex分享个人观察，表示乌鸦能够识别他何时在草坪上播种草籽。
• 1337biz提到有一群人训练野生乌鸦做各种事情，显示乌鸦的聪明才智。
• Domofutu提供了一个相关讨论的链接。
• NanoYohaneTSU讽刺地说训练动物做事情是可以的，质疑这是否已成为媒体报道的大新闻。
• Andoando认为狗和其他有眼睛的动物也能做到，只是兴趣和学习动机的差异。
• Metalman详细描述了乌鸦在建筑物和公路边有条理地觅食的行为，显示其高度的认知能力。

争议焦点：
• 动物智力的比较及其与人类智力的关系是讨论的核心，特别是不同物种间的智力差异是否可以量化，以及如何定义和衡量这种智力。

Crows can recognize geometric regularity
by Bob Yirka										 										 , Phys.org
Intruder detection task. Two carrion crows were trained to detect an intruder stimulus in an array of six simultaneously presented stimuli. The crows initiated the trial by moving their head in front of the screen whenever a go-stimulus appeared. After a prestimulus period of 200 ms, an array of six stimuli was displayed. The crows responded by pecking on the intruder. In 50% of the trials, the crows were tested with non-quadrilateral background stimuli (top); in this example, the crescent is the intruder among stars. In the other 50% of the trials, the crows were tested with quadrilateral probe stimuli (bottom); in this example, a nonsymmetric quadrilateral is the intruder among symmetric quadrilaterals. Credit:
Science Advances
(2025). DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.adt3718
A trio of animal physiologists at the University of Tübingen, in Germany, has found that at least one species of crow has the ability to recognize geometric regularity. In their
study
published in the journal
Science Advances
, Philipp Schmidbauer, Madita Hahn and Andreas Nieder conducted several experiments that involved testing crows on their ability to recognize geometric shapes.
Recognizing regularity in geometric shapes means being able to pick out one
shape
that is different from others in a group—picking out a plastic star, for example, when it is placed among several plastic moons. Testing for the ability to recognize geometric regularity has been done with many animals, including chimps and bonobos. Until now, this ability has never been observed in any creature except for humans.
Because of that, the team started with a bit of skepticism when they began testing carrion crows. In their work, the testing was done using computer screens—the birds were asked to peck the outlier in a group; if they chose correctly, they got a food treat. The team chose to test carrion crows because prior experiments have shown them to have exceptional intelligence and mathematical capabilities.
All the birds tested caught on right away. Each could pick out a star if it was placed within a group of rectangles, for example. To determine their level of skill, the researchers started showing them objects that were only slightly different: one box that was tilted slightly, for example, among others that were not. Their accuracy went down, but it was still much higher than chance.
Example of a canonical probe stimulus layout. Here, a deviant shape (in the top-left position) was placed amid five right hinge reference shapes and had to be recognized as the intruder. Credit:
Science Advances
(2025). DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.adt3718
Continued testing showed that the birds had some understanding of right angles, parallel lines and even some degree of symmetry.
The research team suggests their experiments were quite convincing—the crows were very obviously able to recognize geometric regularity. They note that the experiments also showed that the
birds
could do so with no prior learning. The findings strongly suggest that the ability exists in other animals as well.
(A) Test stimulus set. The crows were tested with a stimulus set consisting of five pairs of nonquadrilateral shapes used as familiar background stimuli that had been used during training (left) and five pairs of quadrilateral shapes used as probe stimuli (right). (B) The five quadrilateral reference shapes used to test deviation from geometric regularity. From left to right, the quadrilaterals increasingly differed in geometric properties (parallelism, symmetry, perpendicularity, equal sides, and equal angles). Here, they are ordered from left to right by decreasing regularity. Credit:
Science Advances
(2025). DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.adt3718

data.title: TikZJax: Embedding LaTeX Drawings in HTML
data.author: steventhedev
data.article_summary: TikZJax 是一个将 TikZ 代码转换为 SVG 的工具。通过在 HTML 文档的 `<head>` 中引入相关 CSS 和 JS 文件，并在 `<body>` 中使用 `<script type="text/tikz">` 标签嵌入 TikZ 代码，浏览器会将该代码编译为 SVG 图形。例如，简单的圆和交换图代码都能被渲染为对应的 SVG。其工作原理是利用 WebAssembly 将 TeX 编译为 Web 可用的格式，通过 PGF 驱动和 dvi2html 将 DVI 输出转换为 SVG，整个过程在浏览器中完成。详细示例和演示可访问 [https://tikzjax.com/](https://tikzjax.com/)。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕TikZJax及其在浏览器中实现LaTeX/TikZ渲染的讨论，涉及技术实现、优缺点以及使用体验。

不同观点：
• [支持与赞赏] ics对Jim Fowler及其Calculus视频的推荐，认为其风格生动有趣，适合复习和学习。同时对TikZJax的实现表示赞赏，认为这种技术破解很有趣。
• [优缺点分析] apetresc对TikZJax的整体印象积极，但指出了多个问题，包括某些核心库功能未实现或出错，存在长期未修复的bug，以及开发者缺乏维护。他还提到构建过程复杂，但仍认为TikZ是最好的图表制作工具之一。
• [技术细节讨论] frumplestlatz对使用“core dump”作为优化手段表示兴趣，并提到了其在其他项目（如Emacs）中的历史先例，同时对在WebAssembly中实现这一方法表示好奇。
• [服务器端渲染偏好] ycombinatrix表示更倾向于在服务器端进行SVG渲染，而非在客户端，暗示对客户端渲染的性能或实用性有所保留。
• [静态SVG生成] xenonite认为生成静态SVG并嵌入静态网页生成器可能更符合一般需求，提供了一个相关技术文章链接。
• [移动端体验] Garlef提到该技术在移动端表现不佳，暗示其在移动设备上的兼容性或性能可能存在问题。
• [怀旧评论] klabetron对Jim Fowler及其在高中介绍的LaTeX表示怀念，个人情感较强，未深入讨论技术细节。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点主要集中在TikZJax的实现细节和实用性上，尤其是功能缺失、bug未修复以及构建过程复杂等问题。
• 对渲染方式的偏好有所不同，部分用户倾向于服务器端渲染，部分用户则认为静态SVG生成更实用。
• 移动端体验和兼容性也被提及，但未深入讨论。

43746831.article_content:
TikZJax
TikZJax converts
script
tags (containing TikZ code) into SVGs.
See a live demo at
https://tikzjax.com/
.
Example
In the
<head>
of your HTML, include
<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="https://tikzjax.com/v1/fonts.css">
<script src="https://tikzjax.com/v1/tikzjax.js"></script>
Then in the
<body>
, include TikZ code such as
<script type="text/tikz">
\begin{tikzpicture}
\draw (0,0) circle (1in);
\end{tikzpicture}
</script>
Your TikZ will be compiled into SVGs; the
<script>
element will be
replaced with the corresponding SVG.  For instance, the above code generates
You can also use this for commutative diagrams.  For example, this code
<script type="text/tikz">
\begin{tikzcd}
A \arrow[r, "\phi"] \arrow[d, red]
& B \arrow[d, "\psi" red] \\
C \arrow[r, red, "\eta" blue]
& |[blue, rotate=-15]| D
\end{tikzcd}
</script>
will be rendered as
How does this work?
Using
web2js
, the Pascal source of
tex
is compiled to WebAssembly; the latex format is loaded (without all the hyphenation data), and
\documentclass[margin=0pt]{standalone}
\def\pgfsysdriver{pgfsys-ximera.def}
\usepackage{tikz}
is executed.  Then core is dumped; the resulting core is compressed, and by reloading the dumped core in the browser, it is possible to very quickly get to a point where TikZ can be executed.  By using an SVG driver for PGF along with
dvi2html
, the DVI output is converted to an SVG.
To emphasize this:
all of this happens in the browser.

data.title: Better Error Handling
data.author: zdgeier
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了错误处理不当所带来的严重后果，如经济损失、空难、人员伤亡等，强调了错误处理在软件安全和可靠性方面的重要性。特别是在TypeScript和JavaScript中，传统的try/catch错误处理方法在简单场景下有效，但在复杂应用中面临挑战，如无法对错误进行类型检查、难以处理限流错误和聚合多个API调用错误等。文章还提到JavaScript允许抛出任何类型的错误，导致类型安全问题。最后，文章指出良好的堆栈跟踪能在一定程度上缓解错误跟踪问题，但传统方法仍存在局限性，需寻找更优的错误处理方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：错误处理的最佳实践和不同编程语言中的错误处理机制

不同观点：
• jackjeff：认为在每行代码后检查错误（如Go语言）是一种糟糕的做法，容易导致开发者忽视错误检查，从而产生难以调试的问题。相比之下，异常机制更为直观，虽然Monad等模式有其优势，但在JavaScript中使用会带来不必要的复杂性。同时，对重试机制持谨慎态度，认为重试可能引发其他问题。
• geocar：反驳认为即使在Rust等静态类型语言中也无法检查和处理所有错误，例如磁盘满错误是无法预见的。主张在多任务环境下通过用户干预解决此类问题，而不是完全依赖代码处理。
• zeroq：通过实际经验说明在已有代码库中引入错误处理和日志记录可能导致代码复杂化，即使从整洁的实现开始，最终也可能变得混乱。
• ivanjermakov：认为将错误作为值处理的方法有其局限性，尤其在函数签名需要更改时，会导致调用链上的每个调用者都需要更新。适合在程序需求明确且正确性优先于原型速度的情况下使用。
• medhir：质疑为何不直接使用.then().catch()处理异步调用中的错误，认为这比引入新模式更符合Go语言的做法。
• RadiozRadioz：指出JavaScript的错误处理本身较差，认为原生支持的类型检查和检查异常能解决许多问题。
• whatsakandr：希望C++默认是`nothrow`，并通过经验说明对不太可能失败的操作使用异常，对更可能失败的操作使用optional。
• kikimora：介绍Common Lisp中的重试机制，并希望现代语言也能引入类似功能。
• pmontra：介绍Erlang/Elixir的错误处理方法，包括返回包含ok或fail值的元组和模式匹配，并指出这些方法在其他语言中可能不适用。
• Animats：强调错误需要有用的分类，以便在捕获错误后知道如何处理，并批评Rust在这方面不够完善。
• eximius：希望语言在错误处理上更加标准化，包括堆栈跟踪、错误包装和多错误组合。
• Lord_Zero：指出“结果模式”在C#中早已存在，并非新概念。
• ChrisMarshallNY：认为最好的错误处理是尽量避免错误发生，通过良好的用户体验设计减少错误率，并在错误发生时以简明和同理的方式报告。
• havkom：主张在合适的代码层次处理特定类型的错误，避免在不合适的层次处理错误以减少代码复杂性和数据不一致问题。

补充讨论：
• 对重试机制的争议：jackjeff和pmontra对重试机制持谨慎态度，认为可能导致其他问题，而kikimora则希望引入类似Common Lisp的重试机制。
• 对JavaScript错误处理的普遍批评：多位评论者（如RadiozRadioz和jackjeff）指出JavaScript在错误处理方面的不足。
• 对错误分类和处理方法的讨论：Animats和geocar强调了错误分类和处理策略的重要性，并提供了实际例子。

通过这些观点，可以看到不同语言和开发者在错误处理上的偏好和实践各有不同，主要争议点在于是否应在每行代码后检查错误、如何有效地处理和分类错误以及如何在语言层面支持这些机制。

43746229.article_content:
Bad error handling has cost billions of dollars, crashed planes, killed people, tanked stock markets, wrecked vehicles, and delayed flights. As we reflect on Halloween, it’s fitting to consider these horror stories of software gone wrong. You can read more about them in my
A Halloween scary story
, based on true events, or watch this newly minted Fireship video.
Thank God I didn’t fly during the CrowStrike incident (see what I did there?).
Error handling isn’t just a technical challenge - it’s a critical aspect of software safety and reliability. Yet in TypeScript and JavaScript, it remains something of a wild west. Today, I’ll share an overview of the current landscape and my preferred approaches.
The Current State of Error Handling
The most common approach is the traditional try/catch method. Everyone is familiar with its basic syntax, which works similarly for both synchronous and asynchronous code:

userId
:
number

=
await
fetchProfileRaw
(userId);
const
posts
=
await
fetchPostsRaw
(userId);
return
{ id: userId, profile, posts };
}
catch
(error) {
throw
new
Error
(
`Failed to fetch user data: ${
error
.
message
}`
);
}
}
While this works well for simple scenarios, it presents significant challenges when scaled to enterprise-level applications or complex libraries.
For the sake of comparison later with other alternative, let’s consider the scenarios of
API Request Chain with Rate Limiting
.
Consider calling multiple dependent APIs where you need to:
Handle rate limit errors specially (by waiting and retrying).
Aggregate errors from multiple calls.
Transform upstream service errors into your API’s error format.
Preserve the original error context for debugging.

Limitations of Traditional Error Handling
Previous I made the analogy that try/catch is akin to GOTO statement, which while some agreed, several disagreed. I also mention the analogy to callback hell without going further, which was under explained. I’ve since retracted these comments as it’s not very relevant to the point and is technically not very correct analogies.
While in my humble opinion that error is harder to follow, I’ve realized that good stack trace significantly alleviates the problem of finding the source of error, and so my argument no longer holds a lot of weight.
1. Type Safety Concerns
While you typically throw Error objects,
JavaScript allows you to throw anything
. This is why in TypeScript, caught errors are typically typed as
unknown

As teams increasingly rely on type-checking for code safety, this limitation becomes more problematic. You can’t be certain what you’re catching, which means your error handling code might itself be prone to errors.

• havkom：主张在合适的代码层次处理特定类型的错误，避免在不合适的层次处理错误以减少代码复杂性和数据不一致问题。

补充讨论：
• 对重试机制的争议：jackjeff和pmontra对重试机制持谨慎态度，认为可能导致其他问题，而kikimora则希望引入类似Common Lisp的重试机制。
• 对JavaScript错误处理的普遍批评：多位评论者（如RadiozRadioz和jackjeff）指出JavaScript在错误处理方面的不足。
• 对错误分类和处理方法的讨论：Animats和geocar强调了错误分类和处理策略的重要性，并提供了实际例子。

通过这些观点，可以看到不同语言和开发者在错误处理上的偏好和实践各有不同，主要争议点在于是否应在每行代码后检查错误、如何有效地处理和分类错误以及如何在语言层面支持这些机制。

data.title: How encryption for Cinema Movies works
data.author: perryflynn
data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了DCI（数字电影先导）电影分发和加密的工作原理。DCI标准定义了从文件格式、加密到放映系统的各个方面，确保电影的安全分发。DCP（数字电影包）包含电影的所有组件，KDM（密钥分发消息）则包含解密影片的加密信息。分发过程中，制片方生成DCP和DKDM（分发KDM），通过AES密钥加密，分发方再将DKDM和证书发送给影院，以验证和放映电影。投影系统包括服务器、媒体块和音频处理器，媒体块负责DRM和解密，确保影片实时解密和播放。DCP格式为包含XML元数据和MXF视频文件的文件夹，命名有特定模式以标识电影的不同属性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数字影院技术，尤其是DCP（Digital Cinema Package）的加密、文件格式、色彩处理以及相关的技术挑战和商业模式问题。

不同观点：
• **支持并推荐深入了解**：andreashaerter 推荐了一位作者在Chaos Computer Club活动中关于数字影院后台的演讲，介绍了数字放映系统、端到端加密、以及如何防止盗版的细节。这提供了对影院技术更深层次的理解。
  
• **技术细节澄清**：asdcplib 作为相关技术库的作者，澄清了DCP的颜色空间、加密方式（逐帧加密而不是整个流加密），以及FPGA在解密、解码、色彩处理中的作用。他还强调DCP是B2B格式，通过合同而非EULA授权，与一般的DRM有所不同。

• **时间线疑惑**：hbcondo714 对文章提到的时间线感到困惑，因为文章链接的讨论是在“昨天”创建的，但规格更新是在2024年，文章本身是去年写的。

• **加密安全性质疑**：dherls 和 jackjeff 对逐帧使用相同AES密钥加密的做法提出质疑，认为这类似于ECB模式，存在安全隐患。jackjeff 建议使用像XTS这样的方法来为每个帧生成独特的密钥。

• **盗版问题讨论**：john01dav 指出，尽管有复杂的加密和DRM保护，盗版电影仍然很容易找到，质疑影院在设备控制权上的牺牲是否值得。

• **水印和反盗版措施的争议**：NoMoreNicksLeft 提到DCP中的水印包含放映系统的序列号，若电影被盗录，影院将面临严重问题。但他也质疑，是否可以通过从不同放映机中导出电影并模糊水印来绕过这一措施。

• **历史技术挑战**：KaiserPro 回顾了2011年时DCP打包的复杂性和硬件需求，指出当时JPEG2000编码需要专门硬件才能接近实时性能。

• **对DRM和标准的批评**：shmerl 批评DRM本质上是为了从参与者身上获取更多利益，尤其是需要购买的标准，暗示整个系统是剥削性的。

• **行业趋势观察**：jeffbee 指出，在2024年美国票房收入下降的背景下，整个影院行业可能正在走向终结。

补充讨论：
• 技术实现的复杂性与历史演变：从早期的硬件需求到现代的解码和处理技术，评论中多次提到技术实现的难度以及随时间的变化。
• 加密安全性与盗版防范的争议焦点：对加密方式的安全性以及水印技术的有效性存在较多质疑和讨论，尤其是对逐帧加密和静态密钥使用的担忧。
• 行业发展趋势：有评论提到了影院行业面临的票房收入下降问题，暗示了技术发展背后更大的商业和行业背景。

43745281.article_content:
How DCI Movie Delivery and Encryption works
31. May 2024
Â·
christian Â·
digital cinema
,
projects
,
reverse engineering
,
security
The Cinema Industry is using its own standards for creating and distributing movies in a secure way. The DCI (Digital Cinema Initiatives) specification defines everything from file formats and encryption to the projection systems itself.
The specification itself is
publicly available
but relies on various IEEE (Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers) and SMPTE (Society of Motion Picture and Television Engineers) standards, which have to be purchased.
Scope
This document will show a rough overview of the DCI workflow and describe in detail how the encryption of a DCI movie works. It will
not
show how to break any encryption and no encryption has been broken while writing this document.
From our perspective, the DCI standard is safe
.
The author of this document has been operating a cinema since 2021, without any insight to the distribution or production side of the industry. Some information may be incomplete.
How itâs started
End of 2023 the movie
WONKA
was released. Some cinemas reported, that they are unable to start this movie on their projector.
The reason was, that a certificate used by the distributor was expired. This certificate was used to sign the DCP files.
The distributor published new files, starting the movie worked again.
Out of curiosity the author started to check how the validation process on the projector is working.
Glossar
DCP
: Digital Cinema Package - A folder which contains all components of a movie. Metadata, Subtitles, Audio and Picture in seperate files
CPL
: Composition Playlist - A DCP can contain multiple audio and video streams which will combined in a CPL
KDM
: Key Delivery Message - A XML file which contains the cryptographical information to allow a movie playback on a specific DCI certified projection system
DKDM
: Distribution Key Delivery Message - Similar to a KDM, but for a remastering or distribution system, not for a projection system
Distribution Process
graph TD
classDef red fill:#a91900
classDef green fill:#126500
classDef purple fill:#650072
legendprod[Producer]:::red
legenddist[Distributor]:::green
legendcine[Cinema]:::purple
legendvendors[Projector Manufacturer]
graph LR
classDef red fill:#a91900
classDef green fill:#126500
classDef purple fill:#650072
dcpcreated(["DCP\ncreated"]):::red --"AES Key"--> dkdmcreated
dkdmcreated(["DKDM\ncreated"]):::red --"encrypted\nAES Key"--> dkdmp
dkdmp[DKDM]:::green --> verify(["Projector\nverified"]):::green
dcpcreated --"to Distributor"--> dcp(["DCP by\nDownload or\nHarddrive"]):::green
distcert["Distributor\nCertificate"]:::green --"to Producer"--> dkdmcreated
verify --"to Cinema"--> kdm[KDM]:::purple
dcp --"to Cinema"--> dcp2["DCP"]:::purple
cinecert["Projector\nCertificate"]:::purple --"to Distributor"--> verify
trusted["Trusted Device List"] --> verify
dcp2 --> projector[Projector]:::purple
kdm --> projector
Projection Systems
Most of the Projection Systems consists of Server, Audio Processor and Projector.
graph LR
server[Server] --> mediablock[Media Block]
hdmi[HDMI Source] --> splitter[Audio Splitter]
splitter --"Video"--> projector
splitter --"Audio"--> sound
subgraph Projector
mediablock --"Video"--> projector[Projector]
end
projector --> screen[Theatre Screen]
mediablock --"Audio"--> sound[Audio Processor]
sound --> speakers[Speakers]
The Server stores the DCPs and KDMs, manages Playlists and controls the Projector and Audio Processor hardware.
Many Cinemas also connect their Theatre Automation (light, curtains, etc.) to the projector. By setting time-based commands into the playlists, lights and screen curtain can be controlled automatically. The Projector Server provides 12V/24V relays for this.
These time-based commands are also used to set the correct Aspect Ratio and Volume on the different DCPs in a Playlist.
The Server can be controlled remotely by a PC or in larger cinemas by a Theatre Management System.
The DCPs are imported from USB/CRU hard drives or by internet download to the server. They are stored encrypted at all times.
The projector includes a so called âMedia Blockâ which handles DRM and decryption. It receives the DCP data and the KDM to decrypt each frame in real time.
On DCP playback the Projector will send the decrypted PCM audio to the Audio Processor which will then send each processed Audio Channel to the respective Speakers.
DCP Format
A DCP is a folder which contains XML metadata files and multiple MXF files for the actual movie.
Folder Naming Pattern
AwesomeMovie_FTR-2_S_DE-XX_DE-16_51_4K_20240119_SMPTE_OV
AwesomeMovie
: A short version of the movie title
FTR
: Media Type, in this case âFeatureâ
2
: Version Number
S
: Aspect ratio, in this case 2.35:1 aka âSopeâ
DE
: Audio Language
XX
: Subtitle Language, in this case is no subtitle available
DE
: Territory
16
: Age Rating
51
: Audio channels, in this case 5.1 surround sound
4K
: Mov

data.title: X-Ray Defence
data.author: fzliu
data.article_summary: 本文是关于国际象棋中的X光防御（X-ray Defence）技巧，作为系列的第二部分，重点探讨如何利用X光防御拯救看似无解的局面。X光防御指的是一个棋子通过另一个棋子间接保护某个关键格子或棋子。文章通过多个实例展示了如何在防守中运用X光技巧，例如在无法直接防守时，通过X光防御间接保护重要棋子或避免被将杀。这些例子逐步增加难度，展示了防守方如何在看似必败的局面中找到隐藏的生机。文章强调，防守技巧在棋艺发展中同样重要，发现这些防守资源可以挽救许多对局。通过这些例子，作者希望展示防守战术与进攻战术一样有趣且关键。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[国际象棋中的防守策略，尤其是X射线防守（X-ray defense）的有效性及训练不足的问题]

不同观点：
• [kazinator的观点]  
  - X射线防守的有效性依赖于特定棋子位置的保护。例如，白方车之所以能防守住，是因为有白方皇后从上方保护它。如果没有皇后的保护，黑方皇后可以直接吃掉白车。  
  - 支持当前棋盘配置中防守线能够穿透敌方棋子的观点，认为这些防守被称为“X射线”是因为它们预见了未来可能的棋局变化（如某个敌方棋子移开后，攻击路线依然有效）。

• [captn3m0的观点]  
  - 认为防守战术和相关的谜题在国际象棋文献和资源中被低估和忽视。  
  - 以Lichess上的Storm模式为例，指出自己虽然擅长发现好的进攻机会，但在防守方面训练不足，导致难以识别好的防守策略。

补充讨论：
• [训练不平衡的问题]  
  - captn3m0提到，很多棋手在训练中更注重进攻而忽视防守，这导致了对防守技巧的掌握不足。  
  - 这种训练不平衡可能导致棋手在实际对局中难以应对复杂的防守局面。

争议焦点：
• [X射线防守的具体条件]  
  - kazinator强调X射线防守的有效性依赖于特定棋子位置的保护，而不仅仅是防守线的穿透能力。这引出了一个问题：在何种条件下，X射线防守才能真正发挥作用？

• [防守训练的不足]  
  - captn3m0指出防守训练资源的不足，这表明在国际象棋教育和资源分配上可能存在偏重进攻、忽视防守的倾向。

总结：讨论主要围绕X射线防守的有效性和防守战术训练不足的问题展开。kazinator具体分析了X射线防守的棋局条件，而captn3m0则从更广泛的训练和资源角度提出了防守被忽视的观点。两者共同指向了防守在国际象棋中的重要性和当前存在的挑战。

X-Ray Defence: Hidden Resource, Sudden Lifeline
Mcie
Apr 17, 2025
72
3,682
views
English (US)
Chess
Analysis
Puzzle
Tactics
Strategy
X-rays that save your position from surprising angles
Todays article is part 2 of 2 in my mini-lesson series on the X-ray motif. This follows up on my previous article which you can find in my blog here on Lichess or in the link for the original article:
X-Ray Attacks: Hidden Pressure, Sudden Impact
. If you haven’t seen that one yet be sure to check it out, as it introduces the theme and covers attacking patterns and puzzles involving the X-ray motif.
While in the first article we explored the offensive potential of the X-ray, in this lesson we flip the board and explore
X-rays as a defensive motif
. This is far less charted but equally important to grasp. As we defined in the previous lesson,
X-rays involve a piece eyeing a square
through
the body of another piece.
Even though the contact in indirect, the influence is still exerted within the line of sight of our piece. We’ve seen how is utilised in attacking themes, but this can work to your favour defensively too! This is demonstrated by the below example:
Defensive X-ray – Introductory Example:
We have to guard Black’s checkmate threat on g2. Rg1 is not available, but there is another defence:
https://lichess.org/study/kWe6Ipj6/rRKXjK1f#0
Rb2 indirectly defends g2 via an X-ray through Blacks Qf2. White’s will survive Blacks attack and will win by material.
In general, defensive tactics and puzzles are underrepresented in chess literature and resources. Probably because brilliant attacks are more satisfying to execute and solve, and defence generally does not attract attention. But learning to spot defensive resources is just as important to our chess development. Every player will be attacked and learning how to survive will save many points.
In the following six examples of gradual difficulty, we’ll explore how an X-ray defence holds the position together when the position looked gloom otherwise. Just like in the introductory example, in each case the defender seems to be in trouble, but a hidden lifeline lurks if you can identify the X-ray motif. Hopefully these examples show that defensive puzzles are just as interesting as attacking ones!
Position 1: Black to move
Black is up a pawn but hadn’t castled and looks to be in a deadly pin. Is it all over or can you find the resource to save the position?
https://lichess.org/study/kWe6Ipj6/8uPj5Ztl#0
Yes!, defensive moves can be pleasing too! Ba4 is the only move to save black, and it is via an X-ray defence of Nc6 through Whites Bishop. The key is to see that Ba4 has indirect contact with Nc6 which becomes direct contact as soon as Whites Bishop takes, and therefore Ba4 does in fact defend Nc6.
Position 2: Black to play
Now Black seems to be in trouble on the back rank. Can Black save the Rook and thereby his King?
https://lichess.org/study/kWe6Ipj6/bgNTDUOs#0
Black could not directly defend his rook but an X-ray defence by Qa8 through Whites Queen saves the day. Note the X-ray defence is mutual, as Re8 also defends Qa8 if White takes the Queen.
The move Qa8 is particularly difficult to spot as it is both X-ray and backwards move, both of which can be blind spots in our tactical visions. If you want more examples of these types of counterintuitive retreating moves, be sure to check out my previous lesson “
Don’t forget about backward moves!
“
Position 3: Black to play
White has sacrificed a piece and is threatening a menacing checkmate on h7. Can it be defended at all?
https://lichess.org/study/kWe6Ipj6/XG7pnvnV#0
Again the only move that holds Blacks position is an X-ray, unconventionally defending h7 via Bd3 through Whites Queen. White’s attack is over and this again shows the importance of indirect line of sight. The next example combines defence and counterattack:
Position 4: White to play
Black has White in check thinking it forces a Queen trade leading to a winning endgame. Do you have a resource in the position?
https://lichess.org/study/kWe6Ipj6/KYPFvZ0L#0
Hopefully the not-so-obvious yet powerful move was not so difficult to find. If this was the case, well done! This is pattern recognition kicking in and your tactical radar gained another weapon to use in your games!
For the final 2 examples I have ramped up the difficulty. There will be more moves to calculate but your tactical visions should be strong and you know what to look for.
Position 5: White to play
This was from my very own game playing White against a 2100+. Black has gone all in with the not-so-subtle plan of Qf3-g2, even leaving their Bd6 to be taken. Can we take it or are we falling into Blacks plan if we do? Or should we look to guard f3 instead?
https://lichess.org/study/kWe6Ipj6/swjFiKlb#0
Yet another incredible save, an X-ray defence of g2 via a8. This example shows that defensive ideas can even win us games if we spot them before our opponent, as it meant we could safely grab Blacks Bishop on d

data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了对TikTok虚拟机（VM）的逆向工程项目，主要目标是解密和反混淆`webmssdk.js`文件。该文件使用了多种混淆技术，如通过数组索引进行变量访问和函数调用，导致代码难以阅读。项目提供了多种工具来反混淆代码、将虚拟机指令反编译为可读形式，并通过脚本注入替换混淆的VM。

文章详细描述了如何处理两种主要的混淆方法：
1. **变量名和函数名的混淆**：通过执行混淆数组代码，还原出原始字符串，再用正则表达式替换代码中的混淆用法。
2. **函数调用的混淆**：将数组中的函数定义替换为标准函数调用，使代码更易读。

项目还解决了虚拟机字节码的解密问题。字节码通过XOR加密存储，解密后可理解VM的工作原理。最终，通过自动化工具和AI的帮助，成功将代码还原为更易读的版本。

data.title: Inside ArXiv
data.author: fprog
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了物理学教授Paul Ginsparg创建的学术资源平台arXiv的故事。arXiv是一个科研论文数字仓库，允许研究人员在论文经过系统评审或验证前分享最新成果。自近35年前成立以来，arXiv改变了科学界的研究分享方式，成为数学和物理学等领域不可或缺的工具。虽然arXiv的论文未经同行评审，但由专家志愿者进行审核以确保基本学术标准。平台的成功展示了科研成果传播可以与评审过程分离，尤其在新冠疫情期间，快速传播了重要研究。然而，arXiv的持续运作面临官僚斗争、过时代码甚至间谍事件的威胁。Ginsparg形容arXiv像一个“离家又回家的孩子”，让他无法完全脱身。尽管如此，arXiv在科学界的重要性不可替代，被誉为改变科学的开创性平台。

• **randomNumber7** 提出，是否有科学家不知道libgen或scihub这些其他获取学术资源的途径，暗示arXiv并非唯一选择。
• **sundarurfriend** 认为文章带有忧郁的基调，反映了维持公共资源（如arXiv）的困难，特别是在服务规模变大后，如何保持其完整性成为一个问题。
• **auggierose** 更喜欢使用Zenodo（由CERN托管），因为其具有更多功能（如访问限制），并且对上传的PDF没有太多限制，相较之下对arXiv有些不满。
• **nickpsecurity** 对arXiv上某些论文的非商业使用许可表示关注，询问如何识别这些论文的许可类型，并对Nature文章的付费墙表示不满。
• **westurner** 提供arXiv支持的文件格式信息，并强调互联网和网络是科学领域最具变革性的平台，支持arXiv的功能和使用。
• **behnamoh** 分享个人经历，指出arXiv因为团队不相信其没有CS学位而长时间搁置其论文，暗示平台在审核方面可能存在偏见。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是arXiv在学术界的角色及其面临的挑战，特别是在维持平台完整性和应对竞争方面。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是不同平台（如arXiv和Zenodo）之间的功能比较，以及对论文许可类型的关注和困惑。
• 个人经历和主观感受（如behnamoh的经历和sundarurfriend的忧郁基调）也为讨论增添了多样性，反映了用户在使用arXiv过程中遇到的实际问题和情绪反应。

“Just when I
thought I was out, they pull me back in!” With a sly grin that I’d soon come to recognize, Paul Ginsparg quoted Michael Corleone from
The Godfather
. Ginsparg, a physics professor at Cornell University and a certified MacArthur genius, may have little in common with Al Pacino’s mafia don, but both are united by the feeling that they were denied a graceful exit from what they’ve built.
Nearly 35 years ago, Ginsparg created
arXiv
, a digital repository where researchers could share their latest findings—before those findings had been systematically reviewed or verified. Visit arXiv.org today (it’s pronounced like “archive”) and you’ll still see its old-school Web 1.0 design, featuring a red banner and the seal of Cornell University, the platform’s institutional home. But arXiv’s unassuming facade belies the tectonic reconfiguration it set off in the
scientific community
. If arXiv were to stop functioning, scientists from every corner of the planet would suffer an immediate and profound disruption. “Everybody in math and physics uses it,” Scott Aaronson, a computer scientist at the University of Texas at Austin, told me. “I scan it every night.”
Every industry has certain problems universally acknowledged as broken: insurance in health care, licensing in music, standardized testing in education, tipping in the restaurant business. In academia, it’s publishing. Academic publishing is dominated by for-profit giants like Elsevier and Springer. Calling their practice a form of thuggery isn’t so much an insult as an economic observation. Imagine if a book publisher demanded that authors write books for free and, instead of employing in-house editors, relied on other authors to edit those books, also for free. And not only that: The final product was then sold at prohibitively expensive prices to ordinary readers, and institutions were forced to pay exorbitant fees for access.
The “free editing” academic publishers facilitate is called peer review, the process by which fellow researchers vet new findings. This can take months, even a year. But with arXiv, scientists could post their papers—known, at this unvetted stage, as preprints—for instant and free access to everyone. One of arXiv’s great achievements was “showing that you could divorce the actual transmission of your results from the process of refereeing,” said Paul Fendley, an early arXiv moderator and now a physicist at All Souls College, Oxford. During crises like the Covid pandemic, time-sensitive breakthroughs were disseminated quickly—particularly by bioRxiv and medRxiv, platforms inspired by arXiv—potentially saving,
by one study’s estimate
, millions of lives.
While arXiv submissions aren’t peer-reviewed, they are moderated by experts in each field, who volunteer their time to ensure that submissions meet basic academic standards and follow arXiv’s guidelines: original research only, no falsified data, sufficiently neutral language. Submissions also undergo automated checks for baseline quality control. Without these, pseudoscientific papers and amateur work would flood the platform.
How to Get Computers—Before Computers Get You
Post-quantum algorithms, thermodynamic hardware, open source architectures, apocalypse-proof programming, and more: WIRED journeys to the freaky
frontiers of modern computing
.
In 2021, the journal Nature
declared arXiv
one of the “10 computer codes that transformed science,” praising its role in fostering scientific collaboration. (The article is behind a paywall—unlock it for $199 a year.) By a recent count, arXiv hosts more than 2.6 million papers, receives 20,000 new submissions each month, and has 5 million monthly active users. Many of the most significant discoveries of the 21st century have first appeared on the platform. The “transformers” paper that
launched the modern AI boom
? Uploaded to arXiv. Same with the solution to the Poincaré conjecture, one of the seven Millennium Prize problems, famous for their difficulty and $1 million rewards. Just because a paper is posted on arXiv doesn’t mean it won’t appear in a prestigious journal someday, but it’s often where research makes its debut and stays openly available. The transformers paper is still routinely accessed via arXiv.
For scientists, imagining a world without arXiv is like the rest of us imagining one without public libraries or GPS. But a look at its inner workings reveals that it isn’t a frictionless utopia of open-access knowledge. Over the years, arXiv’s permanence has been threatened by everything from bureaucratic strife to outdated code to even, once, a spy scandal. In the words of Ginsparg, who usually redirects interview requests to an
FAQ document
—on arXiv, no less—and tried to talk me out of visiting him in person, arXiv is “a child I sent off to college but who keeps coming back to camp out in my living room, behaving badly.”

data.author: xnx
data.article_summary: 2025年3月，美国电力结构中化石燃料占比首次降至50%以下，仅为49.2%。与此同时，太阳能和风能创下新高，合计占美国电力的24.4%，推动清洁能源占比超过一半，达到50.8%。与2015年相比，风能和太阳能的份额增加了四倍多。太阳能发电量同比增长37%，风能增长12%。这标志着美国正接近清洁能源取代化石燃料的转折点，显示出可再生能源在美国能源系统中的主导作用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：可再生能源与化石燃料在电力生产中的现状、成本和未来趋势，以及能源政策的讨论。

不同观点：
• **lambdaone** 认为，电力的批发市场价格受边际发电成本影响显著。目前天然气价格高企，而随着可再生能源（包括储能）承担更多负荷，天然气发电的使用将减少，长期来看有助于降低电价。这一观点强调了可再生能源扩展对经济和电价的积极影响。
• **neallindsay** 指出，推动化石燃料转向可再生能源的主要因素是太阳能板的成本低廉，而非仅仅气候变化问题。这表明经济因素在能源转型中的关键作用。
• **tiffanyh** 提出，尽管可再生能源在满足新增能源需求方面表现出色，但美国化石燃料的总污染量并未减少，只是增长速度放缓。这说明尽管可再生能源增加，化石燃料的使用仍然保持在高位。
• **foobarbecue** 质疑“清洁能源”的定义，指出如果化石燃料（如天然气）被算作“清洁”，可能会误导公众。这涉及到对“清洁能源”标准的讨论和争议。
• **apercu** 表示愿意使用太阳能，但更倾向于从小规模的电池和太阳能设备开始，以替代柴油发电机。这显示了一些消费者对逐步转向可再生能源的实际考量。
• **kylehotchkiss** 提到美国重新启动煤炭开采，质疑煤炭的未来用途，并暗示可能与AI数据中心等新兴需求有关。这涉及到传统能源在新技术领域的潜在应用。

补充讨论：
• **sharemywin** 提到美国对东南亚太阳能板设置高额关税，这可能影响太阳能技术的推广和成本，涉及到国际贸易对可再生能源发展的影响。
• **mugiseyebrows** 询问木材和煤炭用于家庭取暖是否计入污染数据，这涉及到不同能源使用场景下的污染统计问题。
• **gwbas1c** 分享了个人使用太阳能板的经验，指出季节性变化对能源生产和消耗的影响，强调了实际使用中的气候因素。
• **tranchms** 提到能源价格处于历史高位，并提供数据链接，这与lambdaone关于可再生能源降低电价的观点形成对比，显示了当前能源市场价格的复杂性。
• **maxnevermind** 对夏季绿色能源发电量下降表示疑惑，这可能与气候条件和能源需求季节性波动有关。
• **jmyeet** 讨论了能源独立性、温室气体排放以及能源价格上涨等问题，指出公众和市场对能源问题的一些误解，并强调了能源垄断和政策对价格的影响。

争议焦点：
• 可再生能源是否真的能显著降低电价，以及化石燃料在未来能源结构中的角色仍是争议点。
• 对“清洁能源”定义的分歧，尤其是天然气是否应被视为清洁能源。
• 能源价格上涨的原因，部分观点认为与可再生能源有关，而其他观点则认为这是市场结构和政策的问题。

Fossil fuels fall below 50% of US electricity for the first month on record
Record-high solar and wind bring the US to a clean power tipping point
4 Apr 2025
Washington DC, April 4th –
The US hit a new record low for fossil fuels in the electricity mix last month as solar and wind reached a record high, according to new data from global energy think tank Ember. In March 2025, fossil fuels accounted for less than 50% (49.2%) of electricity generated, for the first month on record. This surpasses the previous monthly record low of 51% set in April 2024.
The shift meant that clean sources generated more than half (50.8%) of US electricity for the first month on record. The record was driven largely by an increase in wind and solar power, which reached a record 24.4% of US electricity in March 2025.
In March 2025, US solar power increased a staggering 37% (+8.3 TWh) compared to March 2024. Wind power increased by 12% (+5.7 TWh). Together wind and solar reached an all-time high, generating 83 TWh of US electricity, 11% higher than the previous record of 75 TWh set in April 2024. In comparison, fossil generation fell by 2.5% (-4.3 TWh) compared to March 2024.
Media enquiries
Hannah Broadbent
Director of Communications & Strategy, Ember
[email protected]
Full materials
Media Pack
The milestone is the result of a long term decline of fossil generation in the US power sector, with wind and solar growing substantially over the last decade. Ten years ago, in March 2015, fossil generation still provided 65% of US electricity generation. Wind and solar generation stood at just 5.7%. Since then, the share of wind and solar power has more than quadrupled.
Solar power is set to account for
more than half
of new generating capacity installed in the US in 2025, with more than a third of new solar panels going to Texas. Solar’s rise has been extraordinary. Ten years ago, in March 2015, solar power accounted for just 1% of US electricity generation. By March 2025, this had grown to 9.2%.
Last month Ember published a special report,
US Electricity 2025
, on the changes and trends in the US power sector last year. It found that solar was the fastest and largest growing source of electricity in the US in 2024. Wind and solar power combined rose to a record 17% of the US electricity mix in 2024, overtaking coal for the first time which accounted for 15%.
This clearly demonstrates the growing role of wind and solar in the US energy system. This is a first signal that the US is approaching a tipping point where clean power takes the lead over fossil generation, and where the importance of coal and gas inevitably starts to fade. Wind and solar power are pushing fossil fuels out of the mix. The reality on the ground is not one of a return to fossil fuels in the US, it’s the continued growth of solar and wind power that will be the dominant driver of electricity generation growth in the US.
Nicolas Fulghum
‍
Senior Data Analyst, Ember
About Ember
Ember is an independent energy think tank that aims to accelerate the clean energy transition with data and policy. It creates targeted data insights to advance policies that urgently shift the world to a clean, electrified energy future.

data.title: Taking Notes with Joplin
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: Joplin是一款开源笔记应用，支持多种笔记类型和Markdown语法，具有插件系统和多媒体附件功能。它提供端到端加密同步，用户也可选择仅本地存储。Joplin 3.2版本新增多窗口支持、多列布局、增强的无障碍功能和主题检测。该项目由Laurent Cozic于2016年启动，2022年改为AGPLv3许可证。Joplin支持多平台，包括Linux、macOS、Windows及移动端。它使用SQLite数据库存储笔记，并提供多种导入导出格式。同步功能可通过Nextcloud等WebDAV兼容服务器实现，支持多设备访问和笔记共享。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Joplin及其替代笔记应用程序的优缺点，涵盖功能、文件组织、同步、加密和使用体验等方面。

不同观点：
• **vunderba**：认为Joplin功能不错，但其使用SQLite表和UUID存储笔记的方式不便于使用bash工具或其他IDE处理笔记。相比之下，VS Code、Obsidian、Logseq等应用不改变markdown文件的组织结构，更加方便。
• **joekrill**：推荐SilverBullet，认为其高度可定制且正在积极开发，是目前发现的最好的自托管笔记应用。
• **yesnomaybe**：分享了使用Joplin的经验，提到自托管、跨平台和移动访问功能都能正常工作，但在Arch Linux上遇到一些问题。
• **benwills**：长期使用Joplin，希望其能支持纯文本笔记，而非强制使用markdown或富文本格式。
• **msm_**：自Evernote停止服务后，尝试了多种笔记解决方案，最终选择使用纯markdown文件和git同步，虽然有缺点，但其便携性和通用性强。
• **mattwilsonn888**：对Joplin总体满意，满足了一些基本需求，如markdown和LaTeX支持、文件浏览器等，但未使用到一些高级功能。
• **andrewaylett**：推荐Roam，认为其自动加密和同步功能非常方便，无需手动维护markdown文件。
• **flkiwi**：因Logseq转向APP而选择SilverBullet，尽管不稳定和不精致，但能创建markdown且高度定制化。

补充讨论：
• **exiguus**：十年前选择Joplin，看重其加密、多客户端和自托管能力，并提到可以使用任何编辑器编辑加密后的笔记。
• **brocket**：使用Joplin过程中遇到性能问题，如导入笔记耗时长、移动端无后台同步等，因此在Keep上保存重要笔记。
• **brokegrammer**：自2020年起使用Joplin，通过Syncthing自同步，总体满意。
• **grepfru_it**：推荐Trilium作为笔记应用。
• **I_am_tiberius**：希望Joplin有更好的协作功能，支持团队使用的e2e加密云解决方案。
• **aborsy**：赞赏Joplin的同步功能，并询问是否能根据计划导出所有笔记为markdown以备份。
• **mnls**：认为Joplin是功能最完整的开源笔记应用，支持多平台和e2ee同步。

争议焦点：
• Joplin的笔记存储结构（SQLite和UUID）是否便利。
• 是否需要纯文本笔记的支持。
• 不同笔记应用的自动同步和手动维护markdown文件的优缺点。
• Joplin的性能问题，尤其是同步和导入导出速度。

Joplin
is an open-source
note-taking application designed to handle taking many kinds of notes,
whether it is managing code snippets, writing documentation, jotting
down lecture notes, or drafting a novel. Joplin has Markdown support,
a plugin system for extensibility, and accepts multimedia content,
allowing users to attach images, videos, and audio files to their
notes. It can provide synchronization of content across devices using
end-to-end encryption, or users can opt to stick to local storage
only. Joplin even offers a
command-line
version
for terminal-based usage.
Joplin
3.2
, the most recent feature release, brought long-awaited
multi-window support, multi-column layouts, enhanced accessibility,
and theme detection.
History
Laurent Cozic
started
work
on Joplin in 2016, with an Android version released in July
2017, and the first desktop release (
v0.10.19
)
made available in November 2017. The
complete
changelog
of the project is available on the Joplin web site. The
application is
named in
honor
of ragtime composer and pianist
Scott Joplin
,
whom Cozic admires. More than 650 people have contributed code to the
project over its lifetime; based on the activity
on GitHub
and the steady
stream of releases, it is an active and thriving project.
In 2022, Joplin's user applications
switched
from the
MIT license to the GNU Affero General Public License v3 (
AGPLv3
)
with the 2.9 release. The Joplin project also makes its Joplin Server
available for users who want to run their own synchronization
server. However, that application is released under a
source-available, non-free
Personal
Use License
that forbids commercial use and seems to disallow
modification as well.
Getting started
Joplin is a multi-platform application, with versions for Linux,
macOS, and Windows. It is built with
Electron
for cross-platform
compatibility. Mobile applications are also available for Android and
iOS. It is available for Linux as an AppImage from the
download page
of the web
site. The page also provides instructions for installing the terminal
application and
WebClipper
, a browser
extension for Chrome and Firefox that allows saving web pages directly
to Joplin as notes. The command-line version is not included with the
Joplin download, and is installed using Node.js's npm package manager.
Joplin's editor supports writing content in
Markdown
or using
a Rich Text editor for a
WYSIWYG
experience. However, the project
warns
that the Rich Text editor has some limitations in working with Joplin
plugins that use Markdown. Notes are stored in the Markdown format
whether the user chooses the standard Joplin editor or Rich Text
editor. All notes, notebooks, and attachments are stored in an SQLite
database. Editing with external text editors or file management tools
is possible by selecting "Edit with external editor" from the
application. However, this approach is only feasible when mediated by
Joplin. Directly editing Joplin's notes can disrupt
synchronization.
It also offers an
export
feature
that supports multiple formats, including its own Joplin
Export Format (JEX), as well as JSON, PDF, and plain Markdown, to back
up or transfer data. Similarly, it provides import capabilities,
allowing for migration from other note-taking applications. Users can
import from JEX, Markdown files, and Evernote data via
ENEX
files
while preserving note structure and attachments.
It includes a to-do list function that allows creation and
management of tasks similarly to regular notes. Each to-do item is a
special type of note with an additional "completed" status field. When
creating a new to-do note, users can assign a title, add detailed
content, and set a due date. To-dos can be marked as completed, of
course, which updates their status and changes their sorting order in
the interface, typically moving completed items to the bottom. Notes
themselves can include Markdown to-do lists.
Joplin supports synchronization via a number of FOSS and proprietary
synchronization methods. The easiest open-source option is likely
Nextcloud
, a
widely used self-hosted cloud-storage solution, with synchronization via
its
WebDAV
interface. It requires a properly configured Nextcloud instance and
authentication credentials. WebDAV support extends beyond Nextcloud,
permitting synchronization with any WebDAV-compatible server. This
requires manually entering the server URL and credentials.

data.title: Reworking 30 lines of Linux code could cut power use by up to 30 percent
data.author: gslin
data.article_summary: 文章报道了加拿大滑铁卢大学计算机科学教授Martin Karsten及其团队通过修改Linux系统的30行代码，成功减少了数据中心高达30%的能耗。这一技术调整针对数据中心在处理网络任务时的低效问题，通过优化网络堆栈的运行效率，显著降低了能源需求。该改进对大规模数据中心的节能具有重要意义，有助于减少其对环境的影响。文章强调了技术创新在提升效率和可持续性方面的潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux内核中高性能网络相关的能效优化及其影响

不同观点：
• ryao：支持该补丁，认为它能有效提升数据中心的能效，特别是在非繁忙时段。但批评文章标题具有误导性，可能让人误以为该补丁适用于桌面工作负载。
• hwpythonner：指出许多高性能数据中心工作负载并不通过Linux内核的网络栈，而是使用DPDK、XDP或其他用户空间栈，因此该补丁对这类工作负载无影响。不过，对于内核在数据路径中的设置，该补丁仍然有价值。
• queuebert：从高性能计算的角度出发，认为优化代码以提高能效是一种道德责任，特别是在大规模计算场景下。
• Dwedit：对“高达30%”的能效提升表示怀疑，认为这种表述过于宽泛。
• wrsh07：提到Meta有一种保持GPU忙碌的策略，以稳定电力消耗，指出该补丁可能在某些情况下并不适用。
• linsomniac：回顾了过去的“自适应中断缓解”技术，质疑该补丁是否意味着这项技术不再适用，并分享了自己在处理网络流量突变问题上的经验。
• ssuds：引用关键段落，指出30%的能效提升是最佳情况，实际效果取决于应用对网络的使用频率。

补充讨论：
• 技术链接：corbet提供了关于该变更的详细文章链接。
• 怀旧评论：endorphine和didgetmaster提到阅读相关技术文章唤起了过去的记忆。
• 用户问题：mrbluecoat询问如何启用该节能功能，而mintflow则从使用DPDK技术的经验出发，认为可能存在大量能效浪费。
• 技术优化建议：Jeaye提出是否可以通过重写100行代码来实现改进。

争议焦点：
• 该补丁的适用范围和实际效果存在争议，尤其是在不同类型的高性能工作负载中，其能效提升可能差异显著。
• 标题的误导性引发了对文章理解的讨论，部分读者认为该补丁适用于更广泛的场景，而实际主要针对数据中心。

data.title: Out of the Fog
data.author: wapasta
data.article_summary:
**总结：**

1975年，在美国撤离越南前夕，Operation Babylift（婴儿空运行动）展开，旨在拯救处于战争威胁中的越南儿童。在越战末期，约20,000名儿童生活在孤儿院，许多是混血儿，面临战后报复的传闻威胁。美国政府将此行动包装为人道主义救援，最终将超过2,894名越南和柬埔寨儿童送往美国等国家收养。

行动初期，一架载有200多名儿童的C-5A运输机坠毁，138人死亡，包括78名婴儿。然而，空运行动并未停止，之后更多儿童被送出国，装在卡牌盒中，像行李一样安置在飞机上。尽管行动充满争议，被批评为美国军事失败的遮羞布，但最终这些被收养的儿童在全球各地开始了新生活。如今，这代被收养者仍在处理身份与战争创伤的复杂影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“Operation Babylift”及相关人员（被收养者、养父母等）的经历和媒体报道的分析与讨论

不同观点：
• [jonhohle] 对未获得美国公民身份的被收养者表示同情，认为相关机构在指导流程上存在失误。他强调收养过程本身的复杂性，并指出大多数收养是成功的，虽然存在一些问题案例，但不能以偏概全。他还分享了自己作为养父母的爱与责任感。
   
• [y-curious] 认为文章对“Operation Babylift”的报道过于负面，忽视了行动中积极的一面。他指出，虽然存在问题案例，但并不是所有收养都是负面的，并提到认识的被收养者对他们的经历有不同的看法。

• [randfish] 感谢文章的发布，因为这让他了解了一个与其朋友密切相关的历史事件。他提到其朋友作为被“运送/贩运”的婴儿之一，从未找到亲生父母，显示出对身份认同的困惑与痛苦。

• [camillomiller] 对《The Verge》选择发布此类与科技无关的历史故事感到困惑，认为这偏离了媒体的品牌定位，尽管承认故事本身的重要性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是媒体报道的平衡性，[y-curious] 认为文章过于负面，而忽视了成功收养案例的存在。
• 另一个讨论点是收养过程中的行政失误和公民身份问题，[jonhohle] 特别提到一些家庭因流程不清而未能为被收养者获得公民身份，这引发了对相关机构责任的质疑。
• 历史事件对个人的长期影响也被提及，[randfish] 的评论显示出对历史事件背后个体命运的关注。
• 最后，[camillomiller] 提出了关于媒体内容选择与品牌一致性的技术性讨论，反映了编辑策略与读者期待之间的潜在矛盾。

ï»¿Operation Babylift was an earnest attempt to save children during the fall of Saigon. Decades later, a generation of adoptees wrestles with the aftermath.
In 1975, to hear the Americans tell it, the mass adoption of Vietnamese children was a story of rescue and redemption. These children were war babies, bá»¥i Äá»i, children of dust. A decade of death coupled with a thriving sex trade near US military bases had put nearly 20,000 children in more than a hundred orphanages throughout South Vietnam. By April, as the Viet Cong swept down the coast, mixed race children were said to be in danger. The Northern army would find foreign offspring and carve their livers from their bodies to eat, or so the rumors went. Out of fear and desperation, mothers relinquished their babies â many underweight, sick, or maimed by war â to the Americans. And the Americans took them away.
The popular narrative of Vietnamese adoption began like this:

Aid workers called it a âsalvage operation.â Cherie Clark, a nurse,
recalled
, âWe were literally picking up babies and trying to keep them alive long enough to place them for adoption.â Clark ultimately sent around 1,200 children out of Vietnam through her adoption organization Friends of Children of Vietnam (FCVN).
President Gerald Ford announced Operation Babylift in early April, as it became clear that the US would withdraw its presence from Vietnam entirely. Ford described the babylift as a humanitarian âmission of mercy.â It was, just as importantly, a deflection from military defeat and abandonment. A month later, 2,894 Vietnamese and Cambodian children were on their way to American homes; approximately 1,300 others were adopted to Australia, Canada, and across Europe.
Some of the first children were flown away on a C-5A Galaxy transport aircraft, a plane whose interior could rival a gymnasium. Orphanage workers loaded the cargo hold with 200-plus children, an endeavor âlike trying to carry loose eggs in the bed of a pickup truck,â as journalist Dana Sachs described in her book,
The Life We Were Given
. Twelve minutes after takeoff, a door in the rear of the plane blew out, ripping a hole in the side of the plane. The plane crashed into a rice paddy, crushing the cargo hold where the children were kept â 138 died, including 78 babies.

Operation Babylift continued without a breath. The next day, 324 children, including survivors from the previous dayâs crash, were loaded onto a commercial Pan Am flight. Some babies were buckled into the red-and-yellow plane seats, slumped over like little dolls. 行动初期，一架载有200多名儿童的C-5A运输机坠毁，138人死亡，包括78名婴儿。然而，空运行动并未停止，之后更多儿童被送出国，装在卡牌盒中，像行李一样安置在飞机上。尽管行动充满争议，被批评为美国军事失败的遮羞布，但最终这些被收养的儿童在全球各地开始了新生活。如今，这代被收养者仍在处理身份与战争创伤的复杂影响。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Magic Patterns工具的评价和使用体验，涉及功能、性能、价格以及与竞品的比较。

不同观点：
• [nrmitchi] 对Magic Patterns的整体印象不错，但对响应时间较长表示不满，并认为其"Pro"级别的定价过低，建议将团队功能移至"企业"级别，以实现更高的价值定价。
• [JofArnold] 对Magic Patterns的评价极高，认为其在特定前端设计上表现优异，超越了Anthropic和OpenAI的工具，且在设计和实现方面非常高效。
• [heystefan] 表示Magic Patterns与其现有工具（v0）在某些方面差异不大，仍需多次迭代，不确定是否会切换工具。
• [pedalpete] 对设计和原型作为一次性任务完成的合理性提出质疑，认为迭代过程中编写代码会增加成本和处理时间。
• [sumitkumar] 尝试使用Magic Patterns生成复杂应用时遇到问题，生成的代码无法正常工作，并认为Gemini 2.5 pro在一次性生成方面表现更好。

• [sebastiennight] 认为Magic Patterns可能在UX原型创建和迭代方面与Figma竞争，并询问其是否能重用现有UI组件。
• [mildlyhostileux] 认为Magic Patterns在全新项目中表现良好，但在已有UI的项目中，细节处理和价值体现仍不足。

• 用户对Magic Patterns与Figma等竞品的比较和定位表示关注，特别是在UX/UI原型设计和迭代方面的竞争。

data.title: The Tontine Coffee-House (2018)
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了1792年签署的《梧桐树协议》如何为纽约证券交易所奠定基础，以及一个古老的保险产品和一家同名咖啡馆在这一过程中的作用。在签署协议后，早期的股票经纪人为了避雨，选择在一家名为“唐提咖啡馆”的咖啡馆进行交易。这家咖啡馆的启动资金来源于一种名为“唐提式养老金”的古老保险产品，投资者通过购买股份获得分红，直到去世，剩余收益则分配给存活的投资者，形成一种类似彩票的机制。唐提咖啡馆建成后成为交易中心，并最终演变为纽约证券交易所的前身。1817年，交易活动转移至华尔街40号，唐提咖啡馆后来被改为酒馆、酒店和报社，最终于19世纪中期被拆除。而最初的唐提养老金在1870年结束，仅剩的七名受益者获得了巨额收益。

43752206.article_content:
Those who know a bit about New York’s financial past have almost certainly heard of the Buttonwood Agreement. In 1792, two dozen stockbrokers signed a now famous pact agreeing to trade directly with each other, bypassing any middlemen, under a Buttonwood tree on Wall Street. This agreement standardized trading between them and is thus thought of as setting the foundation for what would become the New York Stock Exchange. But connecting the agreement signed in 1792 to today’s stock exchange on the corner of Wall and Broad is a story involving an antique insurance product and a coffee shop by the same name.
Needing a place to do business outside the rain, Wall Street’s earliest brokers settled on a coffee shop. But no existing one would suffice, a new one, called the Tontine Coffee-House, would be created for the purpose of being New York’s first post-Buttonwood exchange. Where does insurance come into this story; well, the startup capital for the place was provided for by an archaic annuity-like scheme called a tontine.
Tontines
Tontines have a history that goes back long before the Tontine Coffee-House, established on the corner of Wall and Water streets. The scheme, named after a 17th century banker from Naples, Lorenzo de Tonti, combined retirement planning with a lottery; what better way to combine financial savvy with speculative thrill, all the while raising investable capital.
The product worked as follows: Investors each buy shares in the tontine, akin to paying up front for an annuity. The pool of capital is then invested, in a coffee house in the case of our story, and investors receive dividends on their shares until their deaths. Once the number of survivors shrinks to a small group, the investment is wound down.
So far, this looks just like any other annuity; but with a tontine, the distributions that do not go to deceased investors are used to increase the benefits of the surviving ones. This is the lottery part of the scheme. Instead of having to worry about outliving your savings or the decaying buying power of your fixed income with time, with a tontine, living a long life can be very enriching financially. Imagine being among the last handful of survivors in a tontine that started out decades earlier with hundreds of investors; those dividends would look massive compared to the initial investment. You may have had to wait a long time though; knowing how important longevity was to the financial sense of investing in a tontine, many investors named their young children as beneficiaries so as to increase their odds of seeing it to the tontine’s end.
The Coffee-House
Getting back to our story in New York, the tontine that financed the construction of the coffee house had a total of 203 shares sold. Each was $200 in value providing a startup capital of just over $40,000. That’s over $1 million in today’s money, a lot for a coffee shop. While Starbucks is not open to franchisees, some quick research tells me that sum is just about enough to open a Dunkin’ Donuts, so perhaps our inflation calculator really is accurate.
Nonetheless, once built in 1793-94, the Tontine Coffee-House was no ordinary coffee shop; it became a hub for traders in the fast-growing city around it. It may have been no Royal Exchange or
Paris Bourse
then, but in time it would evolve into an exchange bigger than them all. One Englishman quoted a few years later said of the place:
“The Tontine Coffee House was filled with underwriters, brokers, merchants, traders, and politicians; selling, purchasing, trafficking, or insuring; some reading, others eagerly inquiring the news.”
Time and Place
So where exactly was the Tontine Coffee-House? It stood on the corner of Wall Street and Water Street. Paintings and engravings of the three-story building show it on the northwest corner of the intersection, where 82 Wall Street stands today just one block past Deutsche Bank’s New York offices at 60 Wall Street. A 1797 painting by Francis Guy, with the coffee shop located on the far left, shows the masts of ships close by. Back then, Water Street really was by the water; landfills have since expanded the profile of Manhattan by one block in that direction.
The Tontine Coffee-House – painting by Francis Guy
Today, the coffee house is long gone. In 1817, trading moved up the street when the New York Stock & Exchange Board was formed and rented space at 40 Wall Street. The old Tontine Coffee-House would go on to become a tavern, a hotel, and then a newspaper publishing office before being demolished in the middle of the century. The New York Stock Exchange, as it was renamed in the 1860s, moved once more in 1865, and then again to its present location in 1903.
Back to the Tontine
Oh yes, and what about the tontine that started it all? It was wound down in 1870 when the number of beneficiaries was reduced to seven, all of whom were children when the tontine was set up over 75 years earlier. While these lucky seven likely benefited immensely from

data.article_summary: Simon Willison在2025年4月的博客中讨论了基于搜索的研究任务中AI辅助的进展。自2023年初以来，这类工具（如Perplexity和GPT-4驱动的Bing）开始出现，但早期的版本往往产生不准确的信息。到了2025年上半年，Willison认为这些系统终于变得真正有用，尤其是OpenAI的o3和o4-mini，它们能够在回答问题时整合搜索结果，且不容易产生错误信息。相比之下，Google和Anthropic在这方面进展较慢，Google的工具不显示搜索过程，而Anthropic的Claude使用Brave搜索引擎，效果不如Bing或Gemini。Willison还分享了一个实际应用案例，通过o4-mini成功将代码自动升级到新库版本，展示了这种工具的实用性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）和AI工具在搜索、信息验证、实用性等方面的表现和局限。

不同观点：
• **对LLM工具的不信任**：[otistravel] 认为当前的AI工具在处理健康、法律、历史等领域问题时，提供的信息难以验证，是“自信的废话”。他强调真正的AI突破应是能自我承认不确定性并提供引用的系统，而非只是更好的“废话生成器”。
• **实用性与复杂任务处理**：[jonas_b] 希望有一个能比较多种交通方案并按时间排序的聊天机器人解决方案，但不确定当前技术是否能做到。[saulpw] 的实际体验显示，AI工具提供的答案部分有用，但整体效果不如预期，且无法进行更深层次的搜索。
• **深度研究任务的失败**：[CSMastermind] 指出，AI工具在处理特定深度研究任务（如统计NFL球员名单）时表现不佳，无法提供准确答案。[63] 也提到在处理动态搜索和未知因素时，AI工具不够灵活，容易“照搬”谷歌前几条结果。
• **工具的改进与使用体验**：[simonw] 和[sshine] 认为某些LLM系统（如Gemini 2.5 Pro和Kagi）在特定任务上表现有所提升，特别是在长文本理解和多关键词搜索方面。但[blackhaz] 提到，某些模型仍然存在大量“幻觉”问题，即生成不准确的信息。
• **经济与广告模型的影响**：[btbuildem] 担心LLM工具的普及会进一步推动广告模型的侵入性，最终可能导致信息的可信度下降。他希望能有更“干净”的知识获取途径。

补充讨论：
• **LLM作为叙事工具**：[intended] 认为LLM本质上是叙事工具，擅长生成各种风格的内容，但需要用户具备验证能力。专家能有效利用这些工具，因为能判断输出的准确性。
• **Google搜索的变化**：[xp84] 批评Google将搜索顶部位置让给不可靠的LLM生成内容，认为这损害了搜索结果的准确性，并可能导致长期的用户信任问题。
• **选择与整合多种工具的需求**：[sublimefire] 提出，未来的工具应允许用户根据具体任务选择不同的模型和资源，而不是被单一模型限制。

争议焦点：
• **LLM工具的信息可信度与验证问题**：部分用户认为当前的AI工具在处理复杂任务时不可靠，生成内容难以验证；而另一部分用户则认为某些工具在特定领域已取得进展，但整体仍需改进。
• **LLM工具是否能取代传统搜索引擎**：一些用户质疑LLM工具是否能真正替代Google等搜索引擎，特别是在信息准确性和可验证性方面。

43752262.article_content:
Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
AI assisted search-based research actually works now
21st April 2025
For the past two and a half years the feature I’ve most wanted from LLMs is the ability to take on search-based research tasks on my behalf. We saw the first glimpses of this back in early 2023, with Perplexity (first launched
December 2022
, first prompt leak
in January 2023
) and then the GPT-4 powered Microsoft Bing (which launched/cratered spectacularly
in February 2023
). Since then a whole bunch of people have taken a swing at this problem, most notably
Google Gemini
and
ChatGPT Search
.
Those 2023-era versions were promising but very disappointing. They had a strong tendency to hallucinate details that weren’t present in the search results, to the point that you couldn’t trust anything they told you.
In this first half of 2025 I think these systems have finally crossed the line into being genuinely useful.
Deep Research, from three different vendors
o3 and o4-mini are really good at search
Google and Anthropic need to catch up
Lazily porting code to a new library version via search
How does the economic model for the Web work now?
Deep Research, from three different vendors
First came the
Deep Research
implementations—
Google Gemini
and
then OpenAI
and
then Perplexity
launched products with that name and they were all impressive: they could take a query, then churn away for several minutes assembling a lengthy report with dozens (sometimes hundreds) of citations. Gemini’s version had a
huge
upgrade a few weeks ago when they
switched it to using Gemini 2.5 Pro
, and I’ve had some outstanding results from it since then.
Waiting a few minutes for a 10+ page report isn’t my ideal workflow for this kind of tool. I’m impatient, I want answers faster than that!
o3 and o4-mini are really good at search
Last week, OpenAI released
search-enabled o3 and o4-mini
through
ChatGPT
. On the surface these look like the same idea as we’ve seen already: LLMs that have the option to call a search tool as part of replying to a prompt.
But there’s one
very significant
difference: these models can run searches as part of the chain-of-thought reasoning process they use before producing their final answer.
This turns out to be a
huge
deal. I’ve been throwing all kinds of questions at ChatGPT (in o3 or o4-mini mode) and getting back genuinely useful answers grounded in search results. I haven’t spotted a hallucination yet, and unlike prior systems I rarely find myself shouting "no, don’t search for
that
!" at the screen when I see what they’re doing.
Here are four recent example transcripts:
Get me specs including VRAM for RTX 5090 and RTX PRO 6000—plus release dates and prices
Find me a website tool that lets me paste a URL in and it gives me a word count and an estimated reading time
Figure out what search engine ChatGPT is using for o3 and o4-mini
Look up Cloudflare r2 pricing and use Python to figure out how much this (screenshot of dashboard) costs
Talking to o3 feels like talking to a Deep Research tool in real-time, without having to wait for several minutes for it to produce an overly-verbose report.
My hunch is that doing this well requires a very strong reasoning model. Evaluating search results is hard, due to the need to wade through huge amounts of spam and deceptive information. The disappointing results from previous implementations usually came down to the Web being full of junk.
Maybe o3, o4-mini and Gemini 2.5 Pro are the first models to cross the gullibility-resistance threshold to the point that they can do this effectively?
Google and Anthropic need to catch up
The user-facing
Google Gemini app
can search too, but it doesn’t show me what it’s searching for. As a result, I just don’t trust it. This is a big missed opportunity since Google presumably have by far the best search index, so they really should be able to build a great version of this. And Google’s AI assisted search on their regular search interface hallucinates
wildly
to the point that it’s actively damaging their brand. I just checked and Google is still showing slop
for Encanto 2
!
Claude also finally
added web search
a month ago but it doesn’t feel nearly as good. It’s
using the Brave search index
which I don’t think is as comprehensive as Bing or Gemini, and searches don’t happen as part of that powerful reasoning flow.
Lazily porting code to a new library version via search
The truly magic moment for me came
a few days ago
.
My
Gemini image segmentation tool
was using the
@google/generative-ai
library which has been
loudly deprecated
in favor of the still in preview
Google Gen AI SDK @google/genai
library.
I did
not
feel like doing the work to upgrade. On a whim, I pasted
my full HTML code
(with inline JavaScript) into ChatGPT o4-mini-high and prompted:
This code needs to be upgraded to the new recommended JavaScript library from Google. Figure out what that is and then look up enough documentation to port this code to it.

data.title: Show HN: Nerdlog – Fast, multi-host TUI log viewer with timeline histogram
data.author: dimonomid
data.article_summary: Nerdlog 是一个快速、远程优先、多主机的终端用户界面（TUI）日志查看器，具有时间线直方图且无需中央服务器。它灵感来源于 Graylog/Kibana，但更加轻量高效，几乎无需设置。Nerdlog 通过 SSH 连接到远程主机，支持同时从多个主机查询日志，按时间范围和模式过滤日志，并绘制时间线直方图以便快速视觉分析。它不会将日志完整下载到本地，而是在远程节点上分析日志，仅下载部分数据，并通过 gzip 压缩节省带宽。Nerdlog 主要用于查看系统日志（如 /var/log/messages），适用于大文件，并且可以在 Linux 主机上高效运行。虽然仍在概念验证阶段，但其功能可用且速度快。安装需要 Go 语言环境，并可通过 Makefile 构建和运行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 "nerdlog" 项目的功能、优缺点以及潜在改进的讨论

不同观点：
• [piterrro] 认为 nerdlog 项目简洁且采用TUI设计非常酷，并提到自己开发的 Logdy 工具，具有类似的目标但更侧重于网页端、实时日志追踪和多源快速过滤。他指出 Logdy 还不支持多主机查询，但认为 nerdlog 和 Logdy 可以互补。
• [tstack] 赞赏 nerdlog 的界面设计和时间轴直方图功能，并提到从评论中学到了 awk 模式可以结合布尔运算符，而不仅仅是正则表达式。
• [ryanhecht] 指出 nerdlog 不支持 gzipped 日志文件，认为这限制了其使用场景，并询问未来是否有可能支持该功能。
• [Zopieux] 关注 nerdlog 对 journalctl 和 journald 的支持问题，指出项目似乎要求日志以明文形式存储，而其个人不想使用 logrotate 这样的古老方案，倾向于直接使用 journald 的远程日志功能。
• [dloss] 简单表达了对 nerdlog 的赞赏，并将其添加到自己维护的日志查看工具列表中。
• [johnisgood] 询问是否可以在不修改源代码的情况下使用 RFC 3339 时间格式，并询问是否支持 runit（Void Linux）。
• [esafak] 建议开发者寻求社区帮助，将 nerdlog 打包进主流 Linux 发行版以扩大用户群。
• [adityavinodh] 简单表达了对 nerdlog 的赞赏，表示自己正好需要这样的工具。
• [knowitnone] 赞赏项目但指出项目中似乎缺少许可证文件。
• [tomerbd] 询问是否可以查看 AWS CloudWatch 中的日志。
• [nodesocket] 询问是否可以在配置中指定一组共享的日志文件，以便在多个主机上使用。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是 nerdlog 对不同日志格式的支持，特别是 gzipped 日志文件的支持问题（[ryanhecht] 提出）。
• 另一个讨论点是 nerdlog 与 journalctl 的兼容性问题，[Zopieux] 更倾向于使用 journald 的内置远程日志功能，而不是将日志存储为明文（[Zopieux] 提出）。
• 其他多位用户关注 nerdlog 的功能扩展和兼容性问题，例如对 AWS CloudWatch 日志的支持（[tomerbd] 提出）以及多主机日志文件配置（[nodesocket] 提出）。
• 还有一些用户对项目的许可证问题和在特定 Linux 发行版上的支持表示关注（[knowitnone] 和 [johnisgood] 提出）。

Nerdlog
Nerdlog is a fast, remote-first, multi-host TUI log viewer with timeline
histogram and no central server. Loosely inspired by Graylog/Kibana, but
without the bloat. Pretty much no setup needed, either.
It's laser-focused on being efficient while querying logs from multiple remote
machines simultaneously, filtering them by time range and patterns, while also
drawing a timeline histogram for quick visual insight:
Primary use case: reading system logs (
/var/log/messages
or
/var/log/syslog
) from one or more remote hosts. Very efficient even on large log files (like 1GB or more).
It does support some other log formats and can use any log files, but that was the primary use case which was driving the implementation: we were having our web service backend running as systemd services on a bunch of Linux instances, printing a lot of logs, and wanted to be able to read these logs efficiently and having the timeline histogram, much like tools like Graylog have.
Design highlights
No centralized server required; nerdlog establishes an ssh connection to
every node that the user wants to collect logs from, and keeps them idle in
the background (although a separate server to store the log files might still
help in some cases; see the
Requirements and limitations
sections in the article);
Logs are not downloaded to the local machine in full: all the log analysis
is done on the remote nodes, and on each query, only the following data is
downloaded from each node: up to 250 messages from every logstream
(configurable), and data for the timeline histogram. It's obviously possible
to paginate over the logs, to get the next bunch of messages, etc. Nerdlog
then merges the responses from all nodes together, and presents to the user
in a unified form;
Most of the data is gzipped in transit, thus saving the bandwidth as well.
Demo
Here’s a quick demo showing how Nerdlog works across four remote nodes:
Project history
It might be useful to know the history to understand the project motivation and
overall direction, you can read it
here in the full article
.
Project state
Originally hacked together in 2022 to replace painfully slow Splunk setups.
Revisited in 2025 to clean it up to a certain extent, and open source it.
It's still kinda in a proof-of-concept stage though. Implemented as fast as
possible, spaghetti code abounds, could be covered with more tests, a lot more
features could be implemented, etc. Was only tested for real on Linux, and with
Linux hosts to get the logs from.
But it works. It's pretty usable and surprisingly fast.
Installation
To build it, you need
Go
. Having it installed:
To install
nerdlog
binary to your
/usr/local/bin
:
$ make && make install
Or to build and run without installing:
$ make && bin/nerdlog
Usage
When you open the app (
nerdlog
binary), it'll show a query edit form with a
few fields:
Time range is self-explanatory.
Next one is "Logstreams": shortly, a logstream means one or more
consecutive
logfiles like
/var/log/syslog
,
/var/log/syslog.1
etc, on a particular
server accessible via ssh. If you have a server like
myserver.com
accessible
via ssh on port 22, then the logstream to read its
/var/log/syslog
(or
/var/log/messages
) file could be:
myuser@myserver.com
If you need a different port and/or different log files, then a more explicit
form is:
myuser@myserver.com:1234:/some/other/logfile
Multiple logstreams can be provided separated by commas, like this:
myuser@myserver.com, myuser@myserver.com:1234:/some/other/logfile
Nerdlog also reads ssh config (
~/.ssh/config
) and can take the port, username
and hostname from there. It supports globs too, so e.g. in your ssh config you
have two hosts like
myhost-01
and
myhost-02
, then instead of specifying
your logstreams as
myhost-01,myhost-02
it can be simply
myhost-*
.
Obviously though, we can't specify the log files in the ssh config, so if you
need to configure a logstream for non-default log file on some host(s), you can
use the nerdlog's own logstreams config file
~/.config/nerdlog/logstreams.yaml
,
which can look like this:
log_streams:
myhost-01:
hostname: actualhost1.com
port: 1234
user: myuser
log_files:
- /some/custom/logfile
myhost-02:
hostname: actualhost2.com
port: 7890
user: myuser
log_files:
- /some

• [dloss] 简单表达了对 nerdlog 的赞赏，并将其添加到自己维护的日志查看工具列表中。
• [johnisgood] 询问是否可以在不修改源代码的情况下使用 RFC 3339 时间格式，并询问是否支持 runit（Void Linux）。
• [esafak] 建议开发者寻求社区帮助，将 nerdlog 打包进主流 Linux 发行版以扩大用户群。
• [adityavinodh] 简单表达了对 nerdlog 的赞赏，表示自己正好需要这样的工具。
• [knowitnone] 赞赏项目但指出项目中似乎缺少许可证文件。
• [tomerbd] 询问是否可以查看 AWS CloudWatch 中的日志。
• [nodesocket] 询问是否可以在配置中指定一组共享的日志文件，以便在多个主机上使用。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是 nerdlog 对不同日志格式的支持，特别是 gzipped 日志文件的支持问题（[ryanhecht] 提出）。
• 另一个讨论点是 nerdlog 与 journalctl 的兼容性问题，[Zopieux] 更倾向于使用 journald 的内置远程日志功能，而不是将日志存储为明文（[Zopieux] 提出）。
• 其他多位用户关注 nerdlog 的功能扩展和兼容性问题，例如对 AWS CloudWatch 日志的支持（[tomerbd] 提出）以及多主机日志文件配置（[nodesocket] 提出）。
• 还有一些用户对项目的许可证问题和在特定 Linux 发行版上的支持表示关注（[knowitnone] 和 [johnisgood] 提出）。

data.title: Ref Butts and Slam Dunks: What It's Like Photographing an NBA Game
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary:
NBA场边摄影师面临诸多挑战，特别是在视线受阻方面。摄影师Chris Day提到，裁判、教练和球员经常挡住他们的镜头，俗称“裁判臀部问题”。Day自2023年起为《The Commercial Appeal》报社工作，专门报道孟菲斯灰熊队。在NBA季后赛临近之际，他分享了比赛日设备、挑战以及与其他摄影师的合作关系。

Day拥有丰富的新闻摄影实习经验，并在多项摄影比赛中获奖。他使用Sony a9和a7相机，配备16-35mm、70-200mm和300mm镜头。在FedExForum，摄影师有指定位置，比赛期间必须全程坐着，中场休息时才能起身提交照片。

摄影师之间关系友好、互助，常在照片剪裁和选择上互相建议。Day的目标是通过照片讲述比赛故事，捕捉关键时刻、球员和教练的反应。在3月31日的灰熊对凯尔特人比赛中，他专注于新任 interim 教练与球员的互动，以及球迷与凯尔特人球星Jason Tatum的联系。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：体育摄影中的技术与实践挑战，特别是闪光灯使用、设备选择以及工作环境对拍摄的影响。

不同观点：
• **[brudgers]** 认为文章忽略了闪光灯（strobes）在专业体育摄影中的重要性。他指出，闪光灯是专业摄影师拍摄高质量照片的关键，尤其是在美国篮球场馆中，通常会有大规模的共享闪光灯网络。

• **[PaulRobinson]** 分享了一个关于足球摄影师的个人故事，强调了体育摄影工作的报酬和挑战。他提到，自由职业体育摄影师的收入比地方报纸撰稿人要高，但技术难度和工作环境（如在曼彻斯特一月份的户外拍摄）使得这项工作更加具有挑战性。

• **[mrandish]** 提供了关于室内排球摄影的详细技术分析，认为这是最难拍摄的体育项目之一，因为场地照明不足、球员速度快以及镜头和自动对焦系统的限制。他指出，要拍出高质量的照片需要昂贵的设备和大量的尝试，并分享了个人经验和失败后的学习过程。

• **[briandear]** 提供了20世纪90年代作为体育摄影师的经验，强调了当时使用胶片和手动对焦的技术限制。他提到，尽管现代技术进步了，但捕捉“关键时刻”的照片质量并未显著提高。他还分享了使用闪光灯和遥控相机拍摄的经验，并指出自动对焦在当时并不被信任。

补充讨论：
• 闪光灯在体育摄影中的重要性：多个评论提到了闪光灯在不同体育场馆和赛事中的使用，以及其对拍摄效果的影响。
• 自动对焦的可靠性：一些评论者提到自动对焦在复杂场景中可能失效，需要手动对焦来确保照片质量。
• 现代技术与传统技术的比较：讨论了尽管技术进步，但某些传统方法（如手动对焦和胶片摄影）仍然在某些情况下被认为更可靠。
• 室内体育摄影的独特挑战：特别是室内排球和篮球摄影，因照明不足和球员动作快速而增加了拍摄难度。

争议焦点：
• 现代技术是否真正提高了体育摄影的质量：虽然技术进步显著，但一些老派摄影师认为，捕捉关键时刻的照片质量并未因此显著提高。

总结：评论主要围绕体育摄影中的技术与实践挑战展开，涵盖闪光灯使用、自动对焦可靠性、现代与传统技术的比较以及室内体育摄影的独特困难。这些讨论展示了不同年代和不同项目摄影师的经验和观点。

43731335.article_content:
Distance is not a problem. Photographers at NBA games are so close that referees, coaches, and players can block their shots.
“Especially at NBA games, all photographers must face the infamous ‘ref butt’ issue,” says photojournalist
Chris Day
of The Commercial Appeal newspaper. “It differs from game to game depending on the standing habits of the referee, but I certainly have had moments when what I hoped would be a good photo of a Ja Morant dunk was instead a photo of a referee’s dress pants.”
Photographer Chris Day at the Memphis Grizzlies-Boston Celtics game March 31 at FedExForum | Photo by Petre Thomas
Day joined the Gannett-owned Commercial Appeal newspaper in 2023, covering the Memphis Grizzlies of the Western Conference of the NBA. As the NBA playoffs approach (starting April 19 after the play-in tournament April 18), Day shares insights about game-day equipment, challenges, and rapport with other photographers.
Credentials
Day completed four news photography internships from 2019-2022 at the Gainesville Sun, Las Vegas Review-Journal, South Florida Sun Sentinel, and Atlanta Journal-Constitution.
He earned history and journalism degrees from the University of Florida (2020) and a master’s degree from Ohio University’s School of Visual Communication (2022).
At the
2021 Atlanta Photojournalism Seminar
, Day’s work was named Best Student Portfolio. He won second place in 2021 as Student Photographer of the Year in competition sponsored by the Ohio News Photographers Association.
Line of Sight at NBA Games
Line of sight issues cited by Day (“ref butt”) are longstanding. In 2006, Phoenix-based Max Simbron wrote a 10-page
guide
on “Shooting in the NBA” based on his experience photographing the Phoenix Suns.
“… equipment managers, coaches, towel boys, team doctors, and other team people will sometimes put equipment out, and can get in your way,” Simbron advised.
“Referees also roam up and down the baseline. Never expect them to completely be out of your way, you’re just fooling yourself.”
Court Side Logistics
At FedExForum in Memphis, the Grizzlies assign photographers game-day positions.
“We must remain seated the entire time,” says Day, adding that photographers get up at halftime to file and can go on the court when games end.
“I’m rather tall (6’3”), so my legs definitely get real stiff after the long period seated on the ground,” he says.
Players and refs have accidentally stepped on Day’s feet; he has avoided full contact.
“A fellow photographer and I had our hands up to help hold Ja Morant as he started to fall backwards toward us,” Day recalls, “but he luckily caught himself, so we didn’t have to save him from a spill. We both joked that he’s far more valuable than us, and we didn’t want to be known as the photographers who let Ja crash to the ground.”
Equipment
For NBA game assignments, Day uses two cameras (
Sony a9
and
a7
) with a 16-35mm lens, a 70-200mm, and a 300mm.
Chris Day’s equipment goes through a security check at FedExForum, Memphis. | Photo by Chris Day
“For most of the game, the two telephoto lenses are on the cameras as I switch back and forth from shooting the Grizzlies on offense and defense and also scan the crowd for candid reactions,” he says. “At the end of the game, I switch to the wide angle and crouch down to be ready to spring onto the court.”
At FedExForum, a photo room is located near the court.
How do Photographers Treat Each Other?
“We look out for each other,” sums up Day after two years of NBA-game experience in Memphis.
The rapport among photographers is friendly, and supportive.
“I find it enjoyable to be in the photo room with other local photographers,” says Day.
Game-day photographers seek colleagues’ advice on cropping and image selection.
What Are Photographers Looking For?
“My goal,” says Day, “is to tell the story of the game… turning points, great shots, missed shots, and reactions from players, coaches, and fans.”
Grizzlies’ Ja Morant (12) goes for a layup during the game between the Boston Celtics and Memphis Grizzlies at FedExForum in Memphis, Tenn., on Monday, March 31, 2025. | Chris Day/The Commercial Appeal
Anticipation is a key part of the job.
“I hope to get the photos our reporters and editors need before they even ask,” says Day.
For the March 31 Grizzlies-Celtics game (the Celtics won 117-103), Day focused on specific storylines as both teams prepared to enter the playoffs:
Interactions of the Grizzlies new interim coach (Tuomas Iisalo) after the head coach was fired
Connections with fans and players to Celtics star Jason Tatum, born and raised in St. Louis
“During the game I’m following the action but also keep a mental checklist going at all times so I can roam from Tatum to the interim coach to fans who might have Tatum signs.”
Grizzlies’ interim head coach Tuomas Lisalo smiles after talking to Vince Williams Jr. (5) during the game between the Boston Celtics and Memphis Grizzlies at FedExForum in Memphis, Tenn., on Monday, March 31, 2025. | Ch

data.title: Adding keyword parameters to Tcl procs
data.author: BoingBoomTschak
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了在Tcl语言中为`proc`（过程）添加关键字参数（keyword parameters）的功能。作者对某些编程语言缺乏关键字参数以及未向用户提供内置功能感到不满，因此通过几小时的工作，实现了在Tcl中支持关键字参数的方案。文章展示了如何通过包装`proc`来实现这一功能，并给出了具体代码示例，如使用`proc*`定义支持关键字参数的过程，并演示了不同调用方式的结果。此外，作者还比较了使用关键字参数与传统位置参数的性能开销，显示该方法在保持灵活性的同时，性能影响较小。文章最后提到，这种实现借鉴了Tcl中通过强制位置参数来区分选项的特性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Tcl语言中关于添加命名参数功能的讨论和不同实现方案

不同观点：
• jrapdx3 支持使用自己的 nxproc 扩展来实现 Tcl 中的命名参数功能。他认为 nxproc 提供了全面的功能，包括命名参数、位置参数、'rest'参数，以及类型检查等特性。他还提到 nxproc 支持 TclOO（Tcl 对象导向编程），并且提供了跨平台的二进制文件。

• blacksqr 则建议将 OpenACS 工具包中的 ad_proc 过程变成 Tcl 的内置命令。他认为 ad_proc 提供了添加开关、内联文档等实用功能，对 Tcl 开发很有帮助。

• tracnar 提到自己曾经实现过类似的功能，并认为不需要特别的 "quasiquote" 函数，使用 [list {*}$args] 和换行符就能解决问题。他还分享了自己进一步实现的 "pyproc"，可以通过调用 Python 来模拟 Tcl 过程。

• RicoElectrico 提到 Synopsys 工具中通过在值后面跟随名字的方式实现命名参数，例如 `measureFoo $signal threshold 0.9 edge last`。

• andrewshadura 对 Tcl 进行了简要的赞扬，认为 Tcl 作为一种简单、逻辑、一致的 shell 语言，已经做得很好，暗示可能不需要额外的复杂功能。

补充讨论：
• jrapdx3 和 blacksqr 提供了不同的扩展方案，分别代表了外部扩展（nxproc）和内置命令（ad_proc）两种不同的实现路径。
• tracnar 的观点更多是技术实现上的细节分享，提供了对命名参数实现的一种不同思路，同时也展示了与 Python 的交互。
• RicoElectrico 提供的例子展示了其他工具中命名参数的实现方式，为讨论提供了一个参考。
• andrewshadura 的评论相对简单，但代表了一种对 Tcl 现状的肯定态度，可能暗示反对过度复杂化。

争议的焦点：是否需要将命名参数功能内置于 Tcl 中，以及哪种实现方式（外部扩展或内置命令）更为合适。
