Two things that really annoy me with some programming languages: the lack of keyword
(optional, always named and order agnostic) parameters and when the language has a builtin feature
not made available to the user.
Tcl hits the nail here, because a lot of its standard commands have UNIX-like options but
it doesn't make any of this available in either
proc
or
apply
.
But since
proc
can be wrapped "easily" (more later), a few hours gave me
this:
source
.../util.tcl
namespace
path
{::util ::tcl::mathop ::tcl::mathfunc}
proc* p {-flag {-opt foo} x args} {
puts
[lmap v {flag opt x args} {
string
cat
"$v=[set $v]"
}]
}
p 1 a;
# => flag=0 opt=foo x=1 args=a
p -opt bar -flag 1 a;
# => flag=1 opt=bar x=1 args=a
p -flag;
# => flag=0 opt=foo x=-flag args=
#
Relatively constrained overhead
proc
p1
{x} {}
proc* p2 {-flag {-opt foo} x} {}
timerate {p1 1};
# => 0.127049 µs/# 7870986 # 7870986 #/sec 1000.000 net-ms
timerate {p2 1};
# => 0.794317 µs/# 1258943 # 1258943 #/sec 1000.000 net-ms
Pretty nice? As you can see in the third example, I even implemented that Tcl behaviour where
mandatory positional parameter count is used to disambiguate them from options (which is how you
can do
puts $string
without having to safeguard it with a
--
marker).
How it's made
43754004.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了在Tcl语言中为`proc`（过程）添加关键字参数（keyword parameters）的功能。作者对某些编程语言缺乏关键字参数以及未向用户提供内置功能感到不满，因此通过几小时的工作，实现了在Tcl中支持关键字参数的方案。文章展示了如何通过包装`proc`来实现这一功能，并给出了具体代码示例，如使用`proc*`定义支持关键字参数的过程，并演示了不同调用方式的结果。此外，作者还比较了使用关键字参数与传统位置参数的性能开销，显示该方法在保持灵活性的同时，性能影响较小。文章最后提到，这种实现借鉴了Tcl中通过强制位置参数来区分选项的特性。
43754004.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Tcl语言中关于添加命名参数功能的讨论和不同实现方案

不同观点：
• jrapdx3 支持使用自己的 nxproc 扩展来实现 Tcl 中的命名参数功能。他认为 nxproc 提供了全面的功能，包括命名参数、位置参数、'rest'参数，以及类型检查等特性。他还提到 nxproc 支持 TclOO（Tcl 对象导向编程），并且提供了跨平台的二进制文件。

• blacksqr 则建议将 OpenACS 工具包中的 ad_proc 过程变成 Tcl 的内置命令。他认为 ad_proc 提供了添加开关、内联文档等实用功能，对 Tcl 开发很有帮助。

• tracnar 提到自己曾经实现过类似的功能，并认为不需要特别的 "quasiquote" 函数，使用 [list {*}$args] 和换行符就能解决问题。他还分享了自己进一步实现的 "pyproc"，可以通过调用 Python 来模拟 Tcl 过程。

• RicoElectrico 提到 Synopsys 工具中通过在值后面跟随名字的方式实现命名参数，例如 `measureFoo $signal threshold 0.9 edge last`。

• andrewshadura 对 Tcl 进行了简要的赞扬，认为 Tcl 作为一种简单、逻辑、一致的 shell 语言，已经做得很好，暗示可能不需要额外的复杂功能。

补充讨论：
• jrapdx3 和 blacksqr 提供了不同的扩展方案，分别代表了外部扩展（nxproc）和内置命令（ad_proc）两种不同的实现路径。
• tracnar 的观点更多是技术实现上的细节分享，提供了对命名参数实现的一种不同思路，同时也展示了与 Python 的交互。
• RicoElectrico 提供的例子展示了其他工具中命名参数的实现方式，为讨论提供了一个参考。
• andrewshadura 的评论相对简单，但代表了一种对 Tcl 现状的肯定态度，可能暗示反对过度复杂化。

争议的焦点：是否需要将命名参数功能内置于 Tcl 中，以及哪种实现方式（外部扩展或内置命令）更为合适。

data.title: A new form of verification on Bluesky
data.author: ink_13
data.article_summary: Bluesky推出了一种新的验证系统，以增强用户信任。首先，用户可以将域名设置为用户名以进行验证，目前已有超过27万个账户完成此操作。此外，Bluesky将为真实且重要的账户引入易于识别的蓝色勾标记。同时，推出“可信验证者”功能，允许特定独立组织直接验证账户，这些组织的验证标记为扇形蓝色勾。用户可以查看哪些组织授予了验证，并可选择在设置中隐藏验证标记。目前，用户可以通过设置域名作为用户名进行自验证，暂不接受直接申请验证，但未来将开放申请表。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bluesky的验证机制及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **steveklabnik**：对验证机制的技术实现持中立态度。他指出，任何人都可以发布验证记录，但只有被信任的账户会获得蓝标，这类似于技术上的根证书授权（Root CA）。他提到该功能是用户所需求的，并希望该功能能够顺利运行。

• **greyface-**：质疑Bluesky的验证机制与其内部文化愿景（"公司是未来的对手"）是否兼容。他担心如果公司内部出现权力斗争，验证功能可能会像Twitter一样受到影响。

• **gus_massa**：担心验证机制可能被政治实体或不信任的国家用于验证不受欢迎的领导人或大规模验证公民，甚至机器人账户。

• **ajb**：不认同中心化的信任机制，认为这是将信任集中化，而不是反映分布式的社会信任。他主张应由个人决定信任哪些验证者，而不是由Bluesky指定。

• **shrink**：认为使用域名进行身份验证对于非技术人员来说目前不是合适的解决方案，但理解Bluesky选择“信任验证者”的做法是与其价值观一致的。他承认这是一个务实的选择，但不一定是理想的选择。

• **rambambram**：对个人通过自己的网站验证自己并展示蓝标的做法表示怀疑，认为这种做法可能削弱了验证的意义。他更倾向于通过内容本身来判断信息的价值。

• **somat**：认为当前的验证机制优于Twitter的验证，但仍未完全解决问题。他建议跨域验证的解决方案，类似于TLS证书的域验证，但承认一些平台可能不愿意参与这种验证。

• **paxys**：支持信任层级的概念，认为Bluesky验证《纽约时报》，然后《纽约时报》验证其记者，可以使验证过程更具可扩展性。

• **throwawa14223**：认为引入验证机制是反功能的，因为Bluesky的吸引力在于缺乏像Twitter一样的中心化权威。

• **sillysaurusx**：指出许多评论对中心化审核持怀疑态度，但却在一个高度中心化审核的论坛上发表这些评论，认为如果弱审核有积极效果，值得展示。

• **A4ET8a8uTh0_v2**：对验证机制持谨慎乐观态度，认为是大胆的尝试，但担心可能会重蹈覆辙。

• **kristianc**：对验证机制持悲观态度，认为最终可能会导致信任被侵蚀，因为验证标志可能被用于购买地位和冒充他人。

• **FlyingSnake**：认为Bluesky试图回到Elon接手前的Twitter，但可能错失了成为像Signal一样的机会，最终可能只是另一个社交媒体公司。

• **mhh__**：认为旧的蓝标验证机制有助于识别被政权认可的账户，因此对新验证机制持期待态度，尽管他仍在努力适应使用Bluesky。

• **jarjoura**：认为验证机制是限制机器人账户影响力的聪明方式，避免了言论和审查的问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于验证机制是否会导致中心化的信任，以及Bluesky如何在保持去中心化的愿景下有效管理验证过程。
• 验证机制的跨域验证解决方案被认为是更为理想的方式，但实施起来可能面临平台合作的挑战。
• 评论中对中心化审核的态度不一，部分人认为中心化审核在实践中可能具有积极效果，而另一些人则担心其潜在的负面影响。

43753651.article_content:
Trust is everything. Social media has connected us in powerful ways, but it hasn’t always given us the tools to know who we’re interacting with or why we should trust them.
In 2023, we launched our first layer of verification: letting individuals and organizations
set their domain as their username
. Since then, over 270,000 accounts have linked their Bluesky username to their website. Domain handles continue to be an important part of verification on Bluesky. At the same time, we've heard from users that a larger visual signal would be useful in knowing which accounts are authentic.
Now, we’re introducing a new layer — a user-friendly, easily recognizable blue check
. Bluesky will proactively verify authentic and notable accounts and display a blue check next to their names. Additionally,
through our Trusted Verifiers feature, select independent organizations can verify accounts directly
. Bluesky will review these verifications as well to ensure authenticity.
A verified Bluesky account with a blue check.
Trusted Verifiers
Blue checks issued by platforms are just one form of trust. But trust doesn’t come only from the top down; it emerges from relationships, communities, and shared context.
So, we’re also enabling
trusted verifiers
: organizations that can directly issue blue checks. Trusted verifiers are marked by scalloped blue checks, as shown below.
The New York Times account is a trusted verifier with a scalloped blue check.
For example, the New York Times can now issue blue checks to its journalists directly in the app. Bluesky’s moderation team reviews each verification to ensure authenticity.
When you tap on a verified account's blue check, you’ll see which organizations have granted verification.
Tap on the blue check to see which organization verified the user.
You can also choose to hide verification within the app — navigate to Settings > Moderation > Verification Settings to toggle it off.
How to Get Verified on Bluesky
You can self-verify by
setting your domain as your username
. We highly encourage official organizations and individuals to do this.
During this initial phase, Bluesky is not accepting direct applications for verification. As this feature stabilizes, we’ll launch a request form for notable and authentic accounts interested in becoming verified or becoming trusted verifiers.

data.title: Show HN: Dia, an open-weights TTS model for generating realistic dialogue
data.author: toebee
data.article_summary: Dia是由Nari Labs开发的1.6B参数文本到语音（TTS）模型，能够一键生成高度逼真的对话语音。该模型支持基于音频输入控制情感和语气，并能模拟笑声、咳嗽等非语言交流。Dia的预训练模型权重托管在Hugging Face上，并提供与其他模型的对比demo。用户可以通过Gradio UI或命令行工具使用该模型，目前主要支持GPU（PyTorch 2.0+，CUDA 12.6），CPU支持即将添加。Dia初始运行需下载音频编解码器，推理速度取决于GPU性能，完整版需要约10GB显存。该项目遵循Apache-2.0许可证，严禁身份误用、欺骗性内容以及非法或恶意使用。未来计划包括Docker支持、推理速度优化和模型量化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Dia音频模型的技术成就、应用潜力、开源和许可问题以及技术细节和改进建议

不同观点：
• **技术成就和潜力**：
  - hemloc_io和codingmoh认为，Dia模型展示了当前音频模型领域存在大量低门槛的机会，甚至小团队也能与大公司竞争。
  - xbmcuser和eob认为，Dia模型的出现可能颠覆传统配音和有声书行业，带来全新的音频体验。
  - Versipelle期待Dia模型能够实现从EPUB到有声书的转换，并具备多角色、多语调的生成能力。

• **应用和改进建议**：
  - sarangzambare关注Dia模型在实际应用中的延迟问题，并询问是否支持流式输出。
  - a2128和999900000999询问模型的多语言支持情况，特别是非英语语言的训练和使用。

• **开源和许可问题**：
  - strobe提到Dia模型与GNOME项目的命名冲突，并提供了相关链接。
  - rustc关注Dia项目的许可证类型，并指出项目在使用上的限制，特别是身份误用的禁止条款。

• **技术细节和开发背景**：
  - toebee详细介绍了Dia模型的技术特点和开发背景，包括模型的参数、对话生成方式、音频提示支持等。
  - notdian分享了在M2 Pro MacBook上成功运行Dia模型的经验，并提供了代码链接。
  - noiv提到Dia模型的演示页面在书签功能上的有趣实现。

补充讨论：
- tyrauber对Dia团队提供的音频示例表示赞赏，并希望可以直接分享音频链接。
- vagabund指出Dia模型演示页面的链接问题，但对其音频效果表示肯定。

争议焦点：
- 模型的命名与GNOME项目存在冲突（strobe）。
- 模型的多语言支持和训练过程的透明度（a2128, 999900000999）。
- 许可证中的使用限制，特别是身份误用的问题（rustc）。

Dia is a 1.6B parameter text to speech model created by Nari Labs.
Dia
directly generates highly realistic dialogue from a transcript
. You can condition the output on audio, enabling emotion and tone control. The model can also produce nonverbal communications like laughter, coughing, clearing throat, etc.
To accelerate research, we are providing access to pretrained model checkpoints and inference code. The model weights are hosted on
Hugging Face
.
We also provide a
demo page
comparing our model to
ElevenLabs Studio
and
Sesame CSM-1B
.
Join our
discord server
for community support and access to new features.
Play with a larger version of Dia: generate fun conversations, remix content, and share with friends. 🔮 Join the
waitlist
for early access.
⚡️ Quickstart
This will open a Gradio UI that you can work on.
git clone https://github.com/nari-labs/dia.git
cd
dia
&&
uv run app.py
or if you do not have
uv
pre-installed:
git clone https://github.com/nari-labs/dia.git
cd
dia
python -m venv .venv
source
.venv/bin/activate
pip install uv
uv run app.py

A pypi package and a working CLI tool will be available soon.
💻 Hardware and Inference Speed
Dia has been tested on only GPUs (pytorch 2.0+, CUDA 12.6). CPU support is to be added soon.
The initial run will take longer as the Descript Audio Codec also needs to be downloaded.
On enterprise GPUs, Dia can generate audio in real-time. On older GPUs, inference time will be slower.
For reference, on a A4000 GPU, Dia rougly generates 40 tokens/s (86 tokens equals 1 second of audio).
torch.compile
will increase speeds for supported GPUs.
The full version of Dia requires around 10GB of VRAM to run. We will be adding a quantized version in the future.

43754124.article_summary: Dia是由Nari Labs开发的1.6B参数文本到语音（TTS）模型，能够一键生成高度逼真的对话语音。该模型支持基于音频输入控制情感和语气，并能模拟笑声、咳嗽等非语言交流。Dia的预训练模型权重托管在Hugging Face上，并提供与其他模型的对比demo。用户可以通过Gradio UI或命令行工具使用该模型，目前主要支持GPU（PyTorch 2.0+，CUDA 12.6），CPU支持即将添加。Dia初始运行需下载音频编解码器，推理速度取决于GPU性能，完整版需要约10GB显存。该项目遵循Apache-2.0许可证，严禁身份误用、欺骗性内容以及非法或恶意使用。未来计划包括Docker支持、推理速度优化和模型量化。

data.title: FTC takes action against Uber for deceptive billing and cancellation practices
data.author: pinewurst
data.article_summary: 美国联邦贸易委员会（FTC）对Uber采取行动，指控其在未经消费者同意的情况下，擅自将用户加入订阅服务并收费，且设置障碍使得用户难以取消订阅。Uber被指通过这些欺骗性手段进行不正当收费和取消操作。FTC的行动旨在保护消费者权益，要求Uber改变其不当商业行为并可能面临相应处罚。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Uber及其相关服务中的“黑暗模式”、客户服务问题及商业模式的讨论

不同观点：
• paxys和ivape指出Uber通过“黑暗模式”在退款时仅提供账户信用，而不是直接退还到用户的支付方式，且联系客服非常困难。paxys分享了多次与客服交涉才成功退款的经历，而ivape则提到因误解促销活动而未能获得预期优惠，仅获得部分退款。

• laweijfmvo和bilekas批评Uber在取消服务时的复杂流程，例如需要经过多达23个页面和32个操作步骤，这种做法被视为故意让用户难以取消服务。

• jonathanlydall因UberOne的订阅服务导致配送延迟，转而使用本地竞争者，强调本地公司的一致性和较少的资金外流。

• ProfessorLayton建议应立法要求取消订阅的步骤数与订阅时相同，以平衡用户体验。

• dkrich对Uber的商业模式持怀疑态度，认为其盈利能力不足，且因市场压力而采用激进策略。

• Animats提到Uber高管参与政治捐款，暗示这可能影响其商业操作。

• gkapur认为取消UberOne订阅后，通过非订阅用户身份获得更多折扣，质疑UberOne的真实价值。

• rubiquity分享了一次被Uber扣除150美元的经历，因未在规定时间内取餐而失去退款机会，批评其客户服务和商业道德。

• dataviz1000指出不同账户在机场使用Uber时价格不同，建议通过购买本地SIM卡来节省费用，但仍认为Uber比传统出租车更安全。

• superdude12提到Uber在预计接送和送餐时间上经常低估，实际等待时间远超应用显示的时间。

• JohnMakin作为残疾用户，依赖送餐服务，但因一次错误订单和糟糕的客服体验而停止使用Uber，批评其“黑暗模式”和压榨用户的行为。

• YVoyiatzis长期质疑Uber的费用结构，对被曝光的“黑暗模式”感到欣慰，批评公司及其培训的员工接受这种不道德的做法。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Uber通过复杂的取消流程、不透明的费用结构和退款政策等“黑暗模式”获取额外利润，严重影响用户体验和信任。
• 用户对Uber及其相关服务中的客户服务质量普遍不满，特别是在处理退款和取消订阅时遇到的困难。
• 部分用户选择转向本地竞争者以获得更好的服务体验和价格。
• 商业道德和盈利模式的可持续性受到质疑，用户对Uber高管的政治捐款可能影响其商业操作表示担忧。

data.title: LLM-powered tools amplify developer capabilities rather than replacing them
data.author: matthewsinclair
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了大型语言模型（LLM）如Claude Code在编程中的实际作用，指出这些工具更像是增强程序员能力的“机械外骨骼”，而非取代人类程序员。作者通过自己使用Claude Code开发两个应用项目的经验说明，AI工具虽然能大幅加速代码编写过程，但仍需要程序员保持高度警觉，指导工具不偏离方向，并做出关键决策。AI减少了实际编写代码的时间成本，但理解业务问题和设计解决方案变得更加重要。程序员需适应快速生成和丢弃代码的新工作方式，同时保持对整体架构的把控。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编程中的作用及其对开发者的影响

不同观点：
• skydhash认为，传统的编码过程分为三个阶段：理解业务问题、设计解决方案和编写代码。他强调，编写代码本身是最简单的部分，如果在这部分花费过多时间，通常意味着前两个阶段没有做好。他还指出，现代工具和IDE已经大大简化了手动代码编辑的繁琐工作。

• ttul从自身长期的开发经验出发，认为LLM可以帮助开发者快速掌握不熟悉的语言或框架，特别是在理解如何将概念应用到具体框架中非常有帮助。他建议新开发者专注于软件工程的大局观，利用LLM来实现这一目标。

• scrlk强调，成功利用LLM的开发者将是那些掌握这些工具潜力及其局限性的人，LLM的目标是增强人类的能力，而不是取代人类。他还引用“计算机是思维的自行车”这一比喻，讨论了如果人人都能使用强大工具，竞争优势将如何体现。

• Aperocky指出，经验在使用LLM时仍然非常重要，因为LLM可能会犯一些细微的错误或选择错误的方向，只有经验丰富的开发者才能纠正这些问题。

• strict9同意AI可以提高效率，但对一些关于开发者将被取代的夸张说法持怀疑态度。他指出，虽然AI工具可以使任务更容易和更高效，但目前还没有看到任何AI解决方案能真正取代开发者。

• pjmlp认为，LLM的最终目标是外包编程任务，而不仅仅是辅助工具。未来的开发环境将是由计算机内部的系统来完成编程，而不是来自世界另一端的团队成员。

• antirez提出了三种程序员类别：完全依赖AI代理编写代码的程序员、将LLM作为工具手动编写和检查代码的程序员、拒绝使用AI的程序员。他认为，第二类程序员目前具有真正的优势。

• bcrosby95认为，“如何做”的阶段不仅仅是编写代码，而是事先了解如何实现。如果对实现没有十足把握，可以先编写代码，然后根据结果更新自己的理解。

• alganet用比喻说明了当前对LLM的期望与现实之间的差距，期望是开发者内部的机械套装，现实是开发者背上的马鞍。

• Workaccount2质疑，当世界充满了能够快速编写代码的初级工程师时，究竟需要多少和什么样的代码。未来的软件开发将如何变化，特别是当每个人都能使用某种程度的LLM工具时。

• ivape希望未来的开发工具能够像钢铁侠的机甲一样，提供完全的即时反馈和直观的操作体验，而不仅仅是现有的IDE和复制粘贴功能。

• submeta认为，LLM工具放大了开发者的能力，而不是取代他们。他分享了自己的经验，利用LLM工具可以独自完成一个团队的工作，但仍需要人类来管理和审查结果。

• sheepscreek总结，未来的开发环境将是一个人扮演整个团队的角色，包括团队领导、经理，甚至项目经理。这样的能力可以带来高收入，或者选择过一种小而满足的生活。

• causal对LLM和其代理在长时间内难以执行功能性任务的根本原因感到好奇，认为文章没有深入解释这一点。

补充讨论：
• LLM工具对开发者的影响和潜在竞争优势。
• 经验在使用LLM工具时的重要性。
• LLM工具是否会最终取代开发者或只是增强其能力。
• 未来开发工具的理想形态和操作体验。
• 不同类型程序员对LLM工具的接受和使用方式。

[ED: There’s a lot of talk of replacing human programmers. Sure, some will go, but not all. My views on how this plays out have changed considerably over the last 2 months. 3 out of 5 hats.]
Why LLM-Powered Programming is More Mech Suit Than Artificial Human
Last month, I used Claude Code to build two apps: an MVP for a non-trivial backend agent processing platform and the early workings of a reasonably complex frontend for a B2C SaaS product. Together, these projects generated approximately 30k lines of code (and about the same amount again thrown away over the course of the exercise). The experience taught me something important about AI and software development that contradicts much of the current narrative.
The Mech Suit Programmer
Remember
Ripley’s final showdown with the Xenomorph Queen in
Aliens
? She straps into the Power Loader—an industrial exoskeleton that amplifies her strength and capabilities. The suit doesn’t replace Ripley; it transforms her into something far more powerful than either human or machine alone.
This is exactly how tools like Claude Code work in practice. They’re not replacement programmers; they’re amplifiers of what I can already do. That backend project? It would’ve taken me months the old way. With Claude Code, I knocked out the core in weeks. But let’s be clear - I wasn’t just describing what I wanted and watching magic happen.
Think of Ripley controlling that Power Loader. Claude Code gave me tremendous lifting power while I maintained control of where we were going. I made all the architectural calls, set the quality bar, and kept us on vision. Most importantly, I had to watch - diligently - for it going off the rails. And when it did (which happened regularly), I had to bring it back into line. The AI cranked out implementation details at incredible speed, but the brain behind the operation? Still mine, and constantly engaged.
Vigilance Required
With great power comes great responsibility. You must maintain constant awareness when working with AI coding tools—something I learned through several painful lessons.
Claude Code occasionally made bewildering decisions: changing framework code to make tests pass, commenting out whole sections of code and replacing them with hardcoded values to achieve a passing test rather than fixing the underlying problem, or introducing dependencies that weren’t necessary or appropriate. It has a massive bias for action, so you have to ruthlessly tell it to do less than it wants to do to keep it under control. I even found myself swearing at it from time to time in a weird form of anthropomorphising that I am still not entirely sure I am comfortable with or properly understand.
Much like piloting an A380, the system handles tremendous complexity but requires a human to grab the yoke at critical moments. Modern aircraft can practically fly themselves, but we still need skilled pilots in the cockpit making key decisions. Taking your eyes off the process, even briefly, can lead to trouble. In my case, the backend required three complete rewrites because I looked away at crucial junctures, allowing the AI to go down problematic implementation paths that weren’t apparent until much later.
This vigilance requirement creates a fascinating dynamic. While the AI dramatically accelerates certain aspects of development, it demands a different kind of attention from the developer—less focus on writing each line of code, more focus on reviewing, guiding, and maintaining architectural integrity.
The Time Cost of Coding
Working with Claude Code has fundamentally shifted how I think about the economics of programming time. Traditionally, coding involves three distinct “time buckets”:
Why am I doing this?
Understanding the business problem and value
What do I need to do?
Designing the solution conceptually
How am I going to do it?
Actually
writing
the code
For decades, that last bucket consumed enormous amounts of our time. We’d spend hours, days or weeks writing, debugging, and refining. With Claude, that time cost has plummeted to nearly zero. I can generate thousands of lines of functional code in a sitting—something that is, frankly, mind-blowing.
But here’s the critical insight: the first two buckets haven’t gone anywhere. In fact, they’ve become
more
important than ever. Understanding the intent behind what you’re building and clearly defining what needs to be done are now the primary constraints on development speed.
And there’s a new skill that emerges: wielding the knife. With code generation being essentially free, we need to become much more comfortable with throwing away entire solutions. The sunk cost fallacy hits programmers hard—we hate discarding code we’ve invested in, fearing we might break something important or never get back to a working state.

• scrlk强调，成功利用LLM的开发者将是那些掌握这些工具潜力及其局限性的人，LLM的目标是增强人类的能力，而不是取代人类。他还引用“计算机是思维的自行车”这一比喻，讨论了如果人人都能使用强大工具，竞争优势将如何体现。

• Aperocky指出，经验在使用LLM时仍然非常重要，因为LLM可能会犯一些细微的错误或选择错误的方向，只有经验丰富的开发者才能纠正这些问题。

• strict9同意AI可以提高效率，但对一些关于开发者将被取代的夸张说法持怀疑态度。他指出，虽然AI工具可以使任务更容易和更高效，但目前还没有看到任何AI解决方案能真正取代开发者。

• pjmlp认为，LLM的最终目标是外包编程任务，而不仅仅是辅助工具。未来的开发环境将是由计算机内部的系统来完成编程，而不是来自世界另一端的团队成员。

• antirez提出了三种程序员类别：完全依赖AI代理编写代码的程序员、将LLM作为工具手动编写和检查代码的程序员、拒绝使用AI的程序员。他认为，第二类程序员目前具有真正的优势。

• bcrosby95认为，“如何做”的阶段不仅仅是编写代码，而是事先了解如何实现。如果对实现没有十足把握，可以先编写代码，然后根据结果更新自己的理解。

• alganet用比喻说明了当前对LLM的期望与现实之间的差距，期望是开发者内部的机械套装，现实是开发者背上的马鞍。

• Workaccount2质疑，当世界充满了能够快速编写代码的初级工程师时，究竟需要多少和什么样的代码。未来的软件开发将如何变化，特别是当每个人都能使用某种程度的LLM工具时。

• ivape希望未来的开发工具能够像钢铁侠的机甲一样，提供完全的即时反馈和直观的操作体验，而不仅仅是现有的IDE和复制粘贴功能。

• submeta认为，LLM工具放大了开发者的能力，而不是取代他们。他分享了自己的经验，利用LLM工具可以独自完成一个团队的工作，但仍需要人类来管理和审查结果。

• sheepscreek总结，未来的开发环境将是一个人扮演整个团队的角色，包括团队领导、经理，甚至项目经理。这样的能力可以带来高收入，或者选择过一种小而满足的生活。

• causal对LLM和其代理在长时间内难以执行功能性任务的根本原因感到好奇，认为文章没有深入解释这一点。

补充讨论：
• LLM工具对开发者的影响和潜在竞争优势。
• 经验在使用LLM工具时的重要性。
• LLM工具是否会最终取代开发者或只是增强其能力。
• 未来开发工具的理想形态和操作体验。
• 不同类型程序员对LLM工具的接受和使用方式。

GTK LLM Chat
A GTK graphical interface for chatting with Large Language Models (LLMs).
Key Features
Simple and easy-to-use graphical interface built with GTK
Support for multiple conversations in independent windows
Integration with python-llm for chatting with various LLM models
Modern interface using libadwaita
Support for real-time streaming responses
Message history with automatic scrolling
Markdown rendering of the responses
Keyboard shortcuts (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for new line)
Support for fragments:
Include external content (files, URLs, or text snippets) in your prompts.
Conversation Management:
Rename and delete conversations.
Applet Mode:
Run a system tray applet for quick access to recent conversations.
Model Selection:
Choose from different LLM models.
System Prompt:
Set a custom system prompt for each conversation.
Error Handling:
Clear error messages displayed in the chat.
Dynamic Input:
The input area dynamically adjusts its height.
Keyboard Shortcuts:
Enter
: Send message.
Shift+Enter
: New line in the input.
Ctrl+W
: Delete the current conversation.
Installation
pipx install llm               # required by gtk-llm-chat
llm install gtk-chat
System Requirements
llm
Python 3.8 or higher
GTK 4.0
libadwaita
libayatana-appindicator
Usage
Run the application:
llm gtk-applet
or for an individual chat:
llm gtk-chat
With optional arguments:
llm gtk-chat --cid CONVERSATION_ID  # Continue a specific conversation
llm gtk-chat -s "System prompt"  # Set system prompt
llm gtk-chat -m model_name  # Select specific model
llm gtk-chat -c  # Continue last conversation
Development
To set up the development environment:
git clone https://github.com/icarito/gtk-llm-chat.git
cd gtk-llm-chat
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"

The campaign to subvert Africa's internet registry
In ten days, AFRINIC, the continent's internet registry votes in its new board. But one man has been trying to commoditise its resources, and is pushing for a takeover.
ByÂ
Robert Duigan
PublishedÂ
April 15, 2025
A few weeks ago, we were the subject of several cease-and-desist letters, and a lawsuit, for the first version of this article. Due to delays in securing representation, and delays in communication, we were forced to appear in court before we were prepared. In settlement, we agreed to unpublish the initial version without prejudice, leaving open the right to cover the same story in a new form.
This time around, I am writing in a much more dry and clinical style, and ensuring that all factual claims are linked and cited in context, reserving almost all analysis, opinion and speculation until the very last concluding section. This is done merely to avoid confusion about the status of our claims, all of which are linked to sources in context, for which public resources exist. Other claims are backed up by internal sources. We did not err in our assessment of the story below, and the issue is of significant public interest.
Many thanks to those who have reached out to help, and those who have provided information. We now have adequate legal counsel and are confident that we may defend our claims without trouble.
â
In ten days, AFRINIC, an NGO which functions as the internet registry for the African continent, is supposed be holding its regular board elections, but these have been postponed, and await plans from the official receiver who has taken charge of the company. The organisation manages the distribution of IP addresses for the whole African continent, and apportions them to members, rationing what is, for now, a scarce resource to members who pay limited fees at no profit.
The board elections allow a representative from every member organisation (private companies, universities, government bodies) to vote in a governing body. In these elections, a man is contesting for a position on the basis of cancelling its main functions, and privatising the IP addresses, so that they can be sold, rented and traded for profit without regulation.
This man is Chinese citizen Lu Heng.
â
Crash course
IP addresses identify every device connected to the internet, and are vital to its function. There are two protocols - the limited IPv4, and the virtually unlimited IPv6. The world is running out of IPv4 addresses, with the final blocks allocated in 2011. IPv4's 32-bit structure limits it to about 4.3 billion unique addresses, insufficient for todayâs internet demands. The transition to IPv6, with its 128-bit structure offering vastly more addresses, is critical but slow.
Many organizations cling to IPv4 due to compatibility issues, cost, and complexity of upgrading infrastructure. IPv6 adoption is growing slowly, with only 45% adoption globally, and 5% in Africa. Delays in transitioning could lead to a fragmented internet, higher costs for scarce IPv4 addresses, and hindered innovation.
Meanwhile, lucrative trading of IPv4 blocks has emerged, with prices rising as supply dwindles, further complicating access for smaller players. Switching to IPv6 requires careful rationing of IPv4 to allow a buffer zone, and commoditisation would threaten this, and increase scarcity.
Nobody owns IP addresses. They are allocated to members on the basis of registration services agreements (SRAs), wherein users agree to codes of conduct and commit to specific uses, which they must state up front.
This process is managed by the Regional Internet Registries (RIRs). They manage the distribution of Internet number resources (IP address space and Autonomous System Numbers). They include AFRINIC for Africa, The Asia Pacific Network Information Centre (APNIC), the American Registry of Internet Numbers (ARIN), LACNIC, covering South America and the Caribbean, and RIPE NCC for Europe, the Middle East and Central Asia.
Several of these bodies have been approached or targeted in some way by reform campaigns by Lu Heng.
â
What Lu Heng does
Lu Heng is a Chinese citizen who owns Hong Kong based company
Larus
, which rents and âtradesâ the IPs across the globe.
The dwindling supply of IPv4 numbers has stimulated a
lucrative secondary market
for IPv4 addresses, as companies who receive them practically for free (aside from the membership fees to their RIRs, and the occasional service cost) trade them for an average price of around R900 (US$45) each. This is known, in economic terms, as
rentseeking
-
âgrowing one's existing wealth by manipulating the social or political environment without creating new wealthâ
.
In Africa, Lu Heng owns a company called Cloud Innovation, registered in the Seychelles, as a means for gaining access to AFRINIC, which has some of the few remaining free IPv4 bloc

data.title: Tabular Programming: A New Paradigm for Expressive Computing
data.author: dgellow
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了一种名为“表格编程”（Tabular Programming）的新编程范式，灵感来源于m8 Dirtywave音乐序列器。该范式旨在通过一个简约的表格界面来组织代码，每函数限定五个表达式，以促进代码的模块化和可维护性。硬件方面，使用类似Teensy 4.1微控制器，配备小屏幕和八个按钮，无需键盘即可完成编程。

这种设计有以下优点：
1. **减少错误**：通过选择有效选项，避免许多语法错误。
2. **强制分解**：五表达式限制促使函数的细致分解。
3. **明确数据流**：数据流在表格中视觉化。
4. **便携性**：适合随时随地编程。

文中还展示了如何用这种表格编程实现经典的demoscene等离子效果，通过调用初始化和主循环函数来实现效果。这种新范式探索了在硬件约束下如何创造出新的编程环境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：表格化编程环境的适用性和优缺点

不同观点：
• **支持表格化编程的适用场景**：
   - **kats**：列举了一些天然适合表格化表示的场景，如关系型数据库、硬件电路真值表、汇编语言操作码、FPGA编译输出和矩阵乘法等，认为这些场景下表格化编程具有良好的性能表现。但同时指出，将所有应用逻辑都放入表格是困难的，特别是当程序需要频繁扩展或包含复杂功能时。

   - **sedatk**：认为将每个函数限制为五个表达式虽然有助于分解复杂操作，但走向极端会导致代码既不可读也不可维护。作者忽视了过度分解可能带来的问题。

   - **gregschlom**：认为表格化编程类似于汇编语言，所有内容都限制在几列中，但这种方法对可用性不友好。

   - **poulpy123**：认为表格化编程可能仅在某些特定场景（如音乐音序器）中有趣，但在常规计算机中难以找到合适的使用场景。

补充讨论：

   - **gatane**：提到Forth编程语言，暗示这种语言可能与讨论的表格化编程有相似之处。

Tabular Programming: A New Paradigm for Expressive Computing in Constrained Environments
I've been exploring the m8 Dirtywave tracker for a few months now, and it's been a fascinating experience. If you're not familiar with it, the m8 is a portable music sequencer built on the Teensy platform that combines a minimal 8-button interface with a powerful tabular workflow. What makes it special isn't just its portability or its sound capabilities, but how the hardware and interface work together to create an experience that's simultaneously constrained and liberating.
When I'm making music on the m8, I don't feel like I'm fighting with the UI or solving puzzles. It's more like intuitive cooking - mixing ingredients, tasting, adapting, and discovering new flavors along the way. I can lay on my couch, pick it up, and within minutes be immersed in the creative process. No re-learning complicated interfaces, no decision paralysis from too many options - just pure creative flow.
This experience got me thinking about programming environments. Most of our programming tools are designed for desktop workstations with keyboards, mice, and large displays. But what about a programming environment designed specifically for a minimal, portable hardware interface? What would programming look like if it was built around a tabular interface navigated with just a handful of buttons?
The Core Idea
I've been conceptualizing a programming environment built around a tabular interface inspired by the m8. The key insight is that while traditional programming involves typing long streams of text, we could instead organize code into a structured table with each function defined as rows with fixed columns:
NAME: The function identifier
IN: Input parameter specification
EXP1-EXP5: Five expression cells (the core of execution)
OUT: Output specification
At first glance, limiting each function to just five expressions seems incredibly restrictive. But this constraint actually encourages breaking down complex operations into atomic, composable functions - which tends to produce more maintainable code.
The hardware component is just as important as the software model. The target hardware would be deliberately minimal:
Teensy 4.1 microcontroller (same as the m8)
320x240 display
D-pad, A/B, START/SELECT buttons (8 buttons total)
microSD slot and headphone jack
You would navigate the table with the D-pad, edit cells with the A button (which brings up a contextual menu), and run your program with START. No keyboard needed - all programming happens on the device itself through selection rather than typing.
This isn't just about building yet another programming tool - it's about exploring how hardware constraints can lead to new programming paradigms. When you start from the assumption that your interface has just 8 buttons and a small screen, you're forced to rethink fundamental aspects of how programming works.
The current concept is built on a stack-based model similar to Forth, but that's just an implementation detail. The core innovation is the tabular programming model and how it maps to minimal hardware controls.
Some interesting properties emerge from this design:
Error Reduction
: By selecting from valid options, many classes of syntax errors simply cannot happen
Focused Decomposition
: The five-expression limit forces thoughtful function decomposition
Explicit Data Flow
: Data flow between expressions is visually explicit in the table
Portability
: The entire environment is designed for programming on the go, in casual positions

To demonstrate that this concept isn't just theoretical, let's explore how a classic demoscene effect - a plasma - would be implemented using this tabular programming model:

│ PLASMA  │ void│ INIT  │ LOOP  │       │       │       │ void│
│ INIT    │ void│ 0     │ →TIME │ 0     │ →BEAT │       │ void│
│ LOOP    │ void│ TIME+ │ CLR   │ CALC  │ DISP  │ LOOP  │ void│
│ CLR     │ void│ 0     │ VRAM! │       │       │       │ void│
│ CALC    │ void│ 0     │ 0     │ Y-LOOP│       │       │ void│

│ X-LOOP  │ X Y │ PXCALC│ PLOT  │ X 1+  │ X<W?  │ X-LOOP│ void│
│ PXCALC  │ X Y │ X 16/ │ SIN   │ Y 16/ │ COS   │ +     │ VAL │

43751168.article_summary:
本文介绍了一种名为“表格编程”（Tabular Programming）的新编程范式，灵感来源于m8 Dirtywave音乐序列器。该范式旨在通过一个简约的表格界面来组织代码，每函数限定五个表达式，以促进代码的模块化和可维护性。硬件方面，使用类似Teensy 4.1微控制器，配备小屏幕和八个按钮，无需键盘即可完成编程。

这种设计有以下优点：
1. **减少错误**：通过选择有效选项，避免许多语法错误。
2. **强制分解**：五表达式限制促使函数的细致分解。
3. **明确数据流**：数据流在表格中视觉化。
4. **便携性**：适合随时随地编程。

文中还展示了如何用这种表格编程实现经典的demoscene等离子效果，通过调用初始化和主循环函数来实现效果。这种新范式探索了在硬件约束下如何创造出新的编程环境。

data.title: Decentralizing Schemes
data.author: NotInOurNames
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了去中心化社交媒体的优势与挑战，特别是去中心化方案中出现的不良用户体验问题。作者以Fediverse和Bluesky为例，说明用户在不同实例或客户端之间分享和互动时可能遇到的困难。例如，用户点击链接后可能无法直接在当前会话中评论或互动，或者被重定向到默认客户端而非自己偏好的客户端。此外，作者提到帖子迁移和实例关闭可能导致内容丢失的风险。文章还介绍了URI和URL的基本概念，强调去中心化系统需要更好的URI处理方案以改善用户体验。最终，作者指出解决这些问题对于去中心化网络的可持续性和用户体验至关重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：去中心化社交平台中的数据所有权、身份识别和迁移问题，以及不同技术方案的优劣比较。

不同观点：
• WorldMaker支持Fediverse，尤其是Mastodon的实例拥有模式，认为用户应对自己所使用的实例负责，并通过拥有实例来确保内容的所有权。他批评了AtProto和BlueSky的商业模式，尤其是依赖风投资本和潜在的广告业务模式，认为这些模式不如Fediverse可靠。

• Janandonly认为Nostr协议能更好地解决跨实例交互和内容迁移的问题。Nostr使用户的帖子具有可移植性和弹性，因为内容通过公钥和内容哈希识别，而非依赖服务器。此外，Nostr的单一加密身份允许用户在不同中继服务器之间无缝迁移，解决了"帖子便携性痛点"和"迁移痛点"。

• Sambroner分享了自己在Microsoft的Fluid Framework项目中的经验，提出了一种基于URI Schema的设计，可以让应用组件在不同设备和应用程序中进行交互。他强调了这种设计在用户体验和数据交互方面的潜力，但也指出了安全问题是一个主要挑战。

• Immibis回顾了过去的去中心化平台BYOND，指出以前应用通常通过自定义URI方案与网页集成，但随着浏览器内运行应用的能力增强，这种做法逐渐消失。

• Quantadev认为Nostr解决了身份问题，IPFS解决了数据共享问题，但两者未能协同工作是一个遗憾。他还批评了Fediverse中的一些观点，认为将DNS名称嵌入用户名中并不符合自由移动和抗审查的原则。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于不同技术方案的优劣和可行性，尤其是Fediverse、Nostr和IPFS的组合能否实现去中心化社交平台的最佳实践。
• 讨论中还涉及到对内容所有权和用户自由的重视，尤其是如何在技术上实现真正的去中心化和抗审查能力。
• 不同的技术背景和项目经验也影响了参与者的观点，比如Sambroner对URI Schema的偏好和Immibis对历史案例的回顾。
• 对Fediverse社区的一些文化批评（如"超级觉醒"和"喜欢审查"）也显示了技术选择之外的社群动态对技术发展的影响。

43750439.article_content:
Decentralizing Schemes
Search
I’m a fan of decentralized social media and that’s partly because I enjoy using it. But mostly because
history teaches that decentralization is the best basis for sustainable, resilient online
conversation. (Evidence? Email!) For the purpose of this
essay, let’s assume that you agree with me. Let’s also assume that our online life is still Web-flavored.
I’m going to describe a few unfortunate things that can happen in a decentralized world,
then look at a basic built-in feature of the Web that might make the problems go away.
Let’s start with bad-experience scenarios
Sharing pain
·
Suppose I post a picture to my social-media feed and since Ash follows me, it shows up in their stream. They can favorite
or boost it, but let’s suppose they think their friend Layla might like it too, so they grab the link and drop into their chat window
with Layla, or maybe they send her an email.
By “link” I mean “URL”, and by “URL” I mean “URI” (the distinction will matter in a bit). Here’s what that looks like, first
on the Fediverse:
https://cosocial.ca/@timbray/114361121438267145
And on Bluesky:
https://bsky.app/profile/tbray.org/post/3lmxrkmwz5k2u
Layla sees the link and clicks it or taps it and yay, there’s the picture. She dislikes it and wants to add a negative comment.
On the Fediverse, if it turns out she’s logged onto
CoSocial.ca
like me she’ll have no trouble, she can fire away.  If she’s logged into
another instance (and the Fediverse has thousands) she’s out of luck, even though she’s got a live Fediverse session. She can
paste the URL or just “@timbray” into her search window and that might get her there indirectly if she’s lucky.
This is a bad experience.
On Bluesky, it’ll probably just work. Well, for now. Because while Bluesky is based on the
AT Protocol
(ATproto for short) which is in theory decentralized, at the
moment Ash is logged into the “App View” at
bsky.app
just like I am, because in practice everybody
on Bluesky is.
But in a future where there are multiple ATproto App Views, which is to say when Bluesky becomes as decentralized as the
Fediverse is today, we’re back with the Fediverse problem, because her browser doesn’t know that the URI
identifies an ATproto post that she should be able to boost or like.
Client pain
·
There’s another problem in this scenario. Suppose Layla
was
logged into CoSocial.ca, but she wasn’t using the
default Mastodon client, but rather an alternative such as
Phanpy
or
Elk.zone
. When Layla clicks on that link she won’t be in her fave Fedi client but back in vanilla
Mastodon.
Not a good experience.
Post portability pain
·
Let’s look at the URI for a different Fediverse post of a pretty picture:
https://mastodon.cloud/@timbray/109508984818551909
It’s one of my posts all right, but it’s not from
cosocial.ca
, it’s from
mastodon.cloud
, which was my first home on the Fediverse.  I left it in December 2022 because it
was sold to another company which is sketchy, by which I mean
Lolicon
-friendly.
Whatever I think of whoever’s running
mastodon.cloud
, I have a lot of posts over there, some of which I care
about. For now, they’re still there, but I’m not contributing any money to those guys, nor will I, so if they pull the plug and
vanish I can’t complain. Only if they do, so do all those posts that I cared about back then and still do a bit.
Another bad experience.
URIs and schemes
·
[Anyone who already understands URIs schemes and so on can skip to the next section.]
Let’s look at that Fediverse link again:
https://cosocial.ca/@timbray/114280972142347258
I call it a “URI” because that’s the official name for what it is.
What they look like and how to use them are very thoroughly specified
in several Internet Engineering Task Force publications starting with
RFC3986
. URLs are also URIs, but URIs can do surprising things that
you’ve probably never seen in the world of ordinary URLs.
The crucial thing about both the Fediverse and Bluesky URIs is that they begin with the magic letters “https” followed by a
colon. All URIs
begin with a short string and a colon; the string is called the URI
scheme
.  For each possible scheme, there’s a set of rules
saying how to handle URIs of that flavor. If it’s “https”, then the rules say, using that Fediverse URI as an example, to make
an encrypted connection to the server at
cosocial.ca
and ask it to send you
/@timbray/114280972142347258
. You’ll get some bytes that represent what the URI identifies.
[Yes, I’m oversimplifying. Sorry.]
While most of the URLs you’re ever likely to encounter begin with “https:” there are other schemes. Suppose your email is
“tim@example.com”. Paste
mailto:tim@example.com
into your browser, hit Enter, and see what happens.  This is a URI
whose scheme is “mailto” and it works just fine.
When I tried this just now on my Mac, all three of Safari, Firefox, and Chrome noticed that I use the
Mimestream
mail app and popped that up. Which shows that somewhere in this computer there’s
a notion

data.title: Handwriting activates broader brain networks than typing
data.author: onnnon
data.article_summary: 一项发表在《Frontiers in Psychology》的新研究表明，手写在学习中具有不可替代的作用。研究发现，手写相比打字能激活更多且相互连接的大脑区域，尤其在记忆和感官处理相关的区域。手写通过复杂的时空动作刺激大脑，促进视觉、运动和感官输入的整合，而打字主要是重复性按键动作，缺乏这种整合。研究使用高密度脑电图（EEG）对比了手写和打字时的大脑活动，发现手写在大脑中的theta和alpha频段产生了更广泛的连接，这些频段与记忆形成和注意力相关。因此，过度依赖数字工具可能影响学习效果，手写则能独特地促进大脑活动和学习。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：手写与打字对思考、学习和记忆的影响

不同观点：
• 支持手写的观点：
  - [hintymad] 认为手写能够让思维和书写速度同步，从而促进思考，尤其在数学公式书写中更加有效。
  - [sowbug] 提出纸上手写有助于通过“记忆宫殿”效应帮助记忆，记住笔记的位置有助于回忆内容。
  - [kingofheroes] 个人经验表明手写笔记在记忆方面更有效。
  
• 支持打字或质疑手写优越性的观点：
  - [abeppu] 质疑手写是否真的有助于深度思考和错误检查，认为需要更多行为和表现上的证据，提到一项研究未发现手写和打字在单词记忆上有显著差异。
  - [mbrumlow] 认为打字需要的脑力较少，且单指打字无法代表实际打字情况，质疑研究设计的合理性。
  - [NikolaNovak] 强调研究设计不合理，认为应先进行功能性测试，再做脑成像研究。
  - [constantcrying] 强烈质疑脑活动与学习效果之间的关系，认为这些研究没有实际意义和新的见解。
  
• 中立或综合观点：
  - [jakey_2] 认为手写可能激活更多脑区，但也提出记忆效果可能与花费时间有关，而非仅是手写本身。
  - [alganet] 认为手写和打字各有优势，建议综合利用多种方式以最大化脑力活动。

补充讨论：
• 研究设计的争议：
  - 多位评论者（[mbrumlow], [NikolaNovak], [_aavaa_]）指出研究设计存在缺陷，尤其是让参与者仅用单指打字，无法代表实际打字情况，影响了研究结果的可信度。
  
• 个人经验的多样性：
  - 评论中多位用户分享了个人经验，有些人认为手写更有效（[hintymad], [kingofheroes]），而有些人则质疑手写的实际效果（[abeppu], [constantcrying]），显示出个体差异和不同使用场景的影响。

争议的焦点：
• 手写是否真的比打字更能促进深度学习和记忆效果。
• 现有研究的科学性和设计合理性，尤其是关于脑活动与学习效果之间关系的假设。

总体来看，讨论围绕着手写与打字在学习、记忆和思考中的作用，以及现有研究的合理性和实际应用价值。

While keyboards dominate modern classrooms, a new study in
Frontiers in Psychology
suggests handwriting may be irreplaceable when it comes to learning. Researchers found that writing by hand activates far more extensive and interconnected brain networks compared to typing, particularly in regions linked to memory and sensory processing. These findings provide new evidence that handwriting engages the brain in unique ways, raising concerns about the growing reliance on digital tools for education.
As digital tools replace traditional handwriting in classrooms, concerns have arisen about how this shift might impact learning. Typing on a keyboard is often preferred because it enables children to express themselves more quickly and with less physical strain. However, prior research has shown that handwriting is linked to better memory retention, letter recognition, and overall learning outcomes. The fine motor movements involved in handwriting seem to stimulate the brain differently than typing, but the exact neurological mechanisms behind this difference remained unclear.
To investigate, the researchers focused on brain connectivity, which describes how different brain regions work together to accomplish a task. By comparing brain activity during handwriting and typing, the team hoped to uncover whether the physical act of handwriting promotes more extensive brain communication patterns—patterns thought to support learning and memory formation.
“The brain research on handwriting is really a spin-off of our infant brain research in the
NuLab
, our developmental neuroscience laboratory at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), where we show that babies are born with a brain that is ready to learn from day one,” said study author Audrey van der Meer, a professor of neuropsychology.
For their new study, the researchers recruited 40 university students in their early twenties. To ensure consistency, only right-handed participants were included in the analysis, as determined by a standardized handedness assessment. After excluding participants whose data contained artifacts, the final sample consisted of 36 individuals.
Each participant completed two tasks: handwriting and typing. For the handwriting condition, participants used a digital pen to write visually presented words in cursive directly on a touchscreen. For the typing condition, participants typed the same words on a keyboard using only their right index finger. Participants wrote or typed each word repeatedly within a 25-second window while brain activity was recorded. To avoid visual distractions, the words did not appear on the screen during typing.
Brain electrical activity was measured using high-density electroencephalography (EEG), a method that captures rapid changes in brain activity using a net of sensors placed on the scalp. The researchers focused on connectivity, analyzing how strongly different brain regions communicated with each other while participants wrote or typed.
“In our previous studies, critics sometimes mentioned we had tested too few participants,” van der Meer told PsyPost. “This time, we recruited 40 young adults and were able to use the brain data from 36. This is a massive amount of data given that our EEG nets consist of 256 electrodes and can record data at up to 1,000 Hz.”
The results revealed striking differences in brain activity between handwriting and typing. Handwriting activated far more widespread and interconnected brain networks than typing, particularly in the theta (3.5–7.5 Hz) and alpha (8–12.5 Hz) frequency bands. These brain waves, particularly in the lower frequency range, are associated with memory formation, sensory processing, and attention.
The most significant connectivity patterns during handwriting emerged in central and parietal brain regions, which are involved in processing motor control, sensory input, and higher-order cognitive tasks. In contrast, typing produced far less synchronized activity across these areas, indicating that pressing keys involves far less integration of visual, motor, and sensory input than forming letters by hand.
The researchers proposed that handwriting’s benefits arise from the spatiotemporal complexity of the task. Handwriting requires precise coordination of vision, motor commands, and sensory feedback as the brain continuously adjusts finger and hand movements to shape each letter. Typing, on the other hand, relies on repetitive keystrokes that provide minimal motor variation or feedback.
“In our handwriting research, it becomes clear that the brain works differently when writing by hand as opposed to when typing on a keyboard,” van der Meer explained. “Precisely forming letters by hand requires fine motor skills and involves the body and senses to a much larger degree than typing on a keyboard does. As a result, handwriting involves most of the brain, requiring the brain to communicate fast and efficiently between

data.title: Astronomers confirm the existence of a lone black hole
data.author: wglb
data.article_summary: 天文学家首次确认了独立黑洞的存在。由太空望远镜科学研究所的团队牵头，并与圣安德鲁斯大学和欧洲南方天文台的研究人员合作，他们在《天体物理学杂志》上发表论文，描述了如何通过研究多年来收集的数据，特别是2021和2022年的哈勃望远镜数据以及盖亚探测器的数据，确认这一黑洞的身份。此前，该团队在2011年发现了一个“暗天体”，并猜测可能是黑洞，但有其他研究团队认为是中子星。通过进一步研究，该天体质量约为太阳的七倍，排除了中子星的可能性，确认其为独立黑洞。此前发现的黑洞都有伴星，而这是首次确认无伴星的孤独黑洞。研究团队希望借助计划于2027年发射的南希·格蕾丝·罗曼空间望远镜发现更多类似天体。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• [OsrsNeedsf2P] 认为，此前发现的黑洞都有伴星，因此更容易被发现。孤立黑洞由于没有伴星的帮助，很难被观测到。他推测宇宙中可能存在更多未被发现的黑洞。
• [RataNova] 对首次确认孤立黑洞感到震惊，并提出这种黑洞可能大量存在于宇宙中，只是由于不可见而未被发现，除非它们偶然对背景星产生影响。
• [pizzathyme] 对孤立黑洞的存在感到不安，将其形容为漂浮在太空中的" invisible monster"，能够吞噬行星和恒星，暗示了对这种未知天体的恐惧。
• [mirekrusin] 对大爆炸理论与黑洞形成之间的关系感到困惑，质疑小黑洞的存在如何与大爆炸理论兼容。
• [cogman10] 提出一个假设，即这些孤立黑洞是否可能就是暗物质，认为宇宙中可能充满了这些流浪的黑洞。
• [whiteboardr] 对其他人感到惊讶表示不解，认为孤立黑洞的存在应该和那些有伴星的黑洞一样是可能且合理的。

• [wglb] 提供了相关学术文章的链接，为讨论提供了科学依据和背景资料。
• [kleiba] 以拟人化的方式表达了对孤立黑洞的同情。

Astronomers confirm the existence of a lone black hole
by Bob Yirka										 										 , Phys.org
A 2.′′⁡4×2.′′⁡0 WFC3 F814W field showing the OGLE-2011-BLG-0462 field at the final epoch in 2022. The source star and its brighter neighbor are labeled. A faint star lies just to the southeast of the neighbor, but it has little effect on astrometry of the source. For each star, an open green circle shows its location at E1 in 2011, and an open red circle marks its location at E11 in 2022. Stars in this Galactic-bulge field typically move about 1 WFC3/UVIS pixel (0.′′⁡040) over the course of 11 yr. Credit:
The Astrophysical Journal
(2025). DOI: 10.3847/1538-4357/adbe6e
A team of astronomers at the Space Telescope Science Institute, working with one colleague from the University of St Andrews' Center for Exoplanet Science and another from the European Southern Observatory, has confirmed the existence of a lone black hole. In their
paper
published in
The Astrophysical Journal
, the group describes how they studied newer data regarding an object they had spotted several years ago to confirm its identity.
In 2022, members of essentially the same team
reported the discovery
of what they described as a "dark object" moving through the constellation Sagittarius. They suggested it might be a lone black hole. Shortly thereafter, a second research team challenged that result, suggesting it was more likely a neutron star. After continuing to study the object, the original research team has found more evidence backing up their original claim that it is likely a lone black hole.
Prior to this new finding, all the
black holes
that have been identified have also had a
companion star
—they are discovered due to their impact on light emitted by their companion star. Without such a companion star, it would be very difficult to see a black hole. The one identified by the team was only noticed because it passed in front of a distant non-companion star, magnifying its light and shifting its position in the sky for a short while.
The research team made their initial observations using data from Hubble over the years 2011 to 2017. This time around, they looked at data from Hubble for the years 2021 and 2022, as well as from the Gaia space probe. They found that the object under review was approximately seven times as massive as the sun, showing that it could not be a neutron star, leaving only a black hole as the sole option.
Additionally, the second research team
revised their neutron star assessment
in 2023, agreeing that the object was indeed a black hole. They found that the object was around six solar masses, but the higher uncertainty in their measurement still keeps it consistent with the more recent results.
Now, the latest study by the original research team marks the first time the existence of a lone black hole has ever been confirmed. They hope to find more examples with the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, which is scheduled to launch in 2027.
More information:

The Astrophysical Journal
(2025).

43755017.article_summary: 天文学家首次确认了独立黑洞的存在。由太空望远镜科学研究所的团队牵头，并与圣安德鲁斯大学和欧洲南方天文台的研究人员合作，他们在《天体物理学杂志》上发表论文，描述了如何通过研究多年来收集的数据，特别是2021和2022年的哈勃望远镜数据以及盖亚探测器的数据，确认这一黑洞的身份。此前，该团队在2011年发现了一个“暗天体”，并猜测可能是黑洞，但有其他研究团队认为是中子星。通过进一步研究，该天体质量约为太阳的七倍，排除了中子星的可能性，确认其为独立黑洞。此前发现的黑洞都有伴星，而这是首次确认无伴星的孤独黑洞。研究团队希望借助计划于2027年发射的南希·格蕾丝·罗曼空间望远镜发现更多类似天体。

不同观点：
• [OsrsNeedsf2P] 认为，此前发现的黑洞都有伴星，因此更容易被发现。孤立黑洞由于没有伴星的帮助，很难被观测到。他推测宇宙中可能存在更多未被发现的黑洞。
• [RataNova] 对首次确认孤立黑洞感到震惊，并提出这种黑洞可能大量存在于宇宙中，只是由于不可见而未被发现，除非它们偶然对背景星产生影响。
• [pizzathyme] 对孤立黑洞的存在感到不安，将其形容为漂浮在太空中的" invisible monster"，能够吞噬行星和恒星，暗示了对这种未知天体的恐惧。
• [mirekrusin] 对大爆炸理论与黑洞形成之间的关系感到困惑，质疑小黑洞的存在如何与大爆炸理论兼容。

data.title: The Value of Differences: Jennifer Lindsay on Noticing Translation
data.author: Thevet
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了国际文学翻译奖对译者和翻译艺术的认可问题。尽管像国际布克奖这样的奖项提升了译者的地位，增加了他们的知名度，但翻译本身是否得到足够重视仍存疑。文章指出，译者通常出于对语言和文化的热爱从事翻译工作，而非为了名利。虽然奖项让译者更显眼，但这些奖项主要鼓励英国和爱尔兰的出版社出版更多翻译作品，且侧重于近年出版的书籍，忽视了重译作品。布克奖和国际布克奖强调对称关系，使翻译作品与原创作品看似无异，某种程度上模糊了翻译的独特性，使得翻译过程本身被低估。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：翻译中如何处理原语言文化的表达和翻译的“感觉”

不同观点：
• [jbjbjbjb的观点] 他们认为翻译不应抹去原语言的特色，特别是习语部分。读者希望看到原语言的独特之处在翻译中有所体现，而不是让译文完全流畅到让人感觉不到原文是非英语的。这种观点强调了保留原语言文化特色的重要性。

• [nestorD的观点] 作为有经验的翻译者，nestorD指出很多翻译作品，尤其是非小说类，甚至有些小说类的作品，会有一种“被翻译的感觉”。这种感受让读者意识到翻译的存在，表明翻译不仅仅是两种语言的转换，更是一项需要专业技能的工作。nestorD强调翻译的技艺性，认为翻译不应完全隐藏译者的工作。

补充讨论：
• [翻译中的文化保留] jbjbjbjb希望看到原语言文化在翻译中被“庆祝”，这涉及到翻译中如何处理文化特性的问题。他们强调了习语等文化元素在翻译中应得到特别的关注和保留。

• [翻译的专业性] nestorD通过自身的翻译经验指出，翻译作品往往会带有一种“被翻译的痕迹”，这并不是翻译的失败，而是翻译工作复杂性的体现。他们认为好的翻译需要体现出翻译的技巧和难度，而不是完全隐藏翻译的痕迹。

争议焦点：
• 翻译时是否应尽量消除“翻译的感觉”，使译文读起来像原文就是用目标语言写成的，还是应保留一些原语言的特色和翻译的痕迹以体现文化的多样性和翻译的艺术性。

43755682.article_content:
Info
Topics
On translation
,
Literary criticism
Writers
Jennifer Lindsay
Footnotes
Full disclosure here: I have twice been short-listed for this prize, and once invited to be on the jury, which I declined.
My time frame was not rigid, as the number of issues per year vary:
NYRB
20;
LRB
24;
ABR
11. I extended the time frame for the
ABR
to 2022-2023 to make it more equivalent.
International literary prizes and book reviews are increasingly acknowledging the importance of translated work. However, as Jennifer Lindsay argues, while translators themselves are receiving acclaim, their art remains largely underappreciated.
Translators are usually passionate about language - their own and others’ - and about other places. You don’t sink into a translation project, which can take at least a year or two out of your life, to get attention or to earn big money. Appreciation is satisfying, though - not necessarily for oneself, but for the art. Translation prizes and book reviews are where you expect such appreciation to be found. Someone noticed.
When in 2015 the Booker Prize Foundation announced that, from 2016 onwards, the Man Booker International Prize, which had been awarded every second year to an author for their entire body of work, was to be reborn as the International Booker Prize for fiction in translation, translators welcomed this as a sign of growing appreciation for their art. The generous prize money of £50,000 for a single book was to be shared between translator and author. So far, nine awards have been given – to books originally written in Korean, Hebrew, Polish, Arabic, Dutch, French, Hindi, Bulgarian and German. Their translators have received acclaim, and the prize has helped other translators step out from invisibility. Increasingly, they are credited, named on book covers, sought by publishers, and receive better contractual terms. The IBP has also influenced other translation prizes worldwide.
But how much have things really progressed? While the International Booker might have heralded a rise in the status of literary translators, is there a commensurate deepening of appreciation for, and understanding of, translation itself? While translators are being made more visible, is translation being made more invisible?
What is it that gets rewarded, targeted, and neglected by translation prizes? Let us stay with the International Booker. The prize is limited to books translated into English. (For the sake of comparison, a study of international prizes for translation into languages other than English is sorely needed). Entries must be books published (or co-published) in the UK or Ireland, and submissions be made by publishers. The translation must have been published within a one-year period (May-April) prior to the closing date. The prize is annual.
In its 2021 press release, the Prize
stated
that its aim is ‘to encourage more reading of quality fiction from all over the world’. So far, so good, but that noble aim is significantly qualified when the criteria are scrutinised. First, it is clearly a prize intended to encourage British publishers to publish more literature in translation. They submit entries not just because of an altruistic motive of nurturing translation, but also because a win or a short-list nomination significantly lifts sales. Fair enough. Second, the prize – like the main Booker Prize, which is awarded to an original work of fiction written in English – targets recent books. For the International Booker, however,
both
author and translator must be living at the time of submission, thereby favouring books that are also recently published in their original language. In short, the English language publisher is looking for a ‘new book’. Third, while I could find no explicit stipulation on this, the prize does not appear to promote re-translations. Clearly, this disqualifies a lot of international ‘quality fiction’.
When I accessed the Booker Prizes website in December 2024, it
stressed
the equivalence of the Booker Prize and the International Booker Prize:
The symmetrical relationship between the Booker Prize and the International Booker Prize ensures that the Booker honours fiction on a global basis: world-class fiction is highlighted by the prizes for English-speaking readers, whether that work was originally written in English (the Booker Prize) or translated into English (the International Booker Prize).
Media releases for the IBP winners also stress ‘this symmetrical relationship’, blurring the uniqueness of translated work, and, one might say, blurring translation. Despite the elevation of the translator to co-prizewinner, translation itself appears almost incidental. I am struck by how little specific comment there is on it. The emphasis is on ‘the book’ – new, disturbing, pathbreaking, original, lyrical, shocking, powerful, or beautiful. It is almost as though translation is downplayed in order for the book to be accepted as something on par with fiction originally written

data.title: Blog hosted on a Nintendo Wii
data.author: edent
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者在一个任天堂Wii游戏机上运行NetBSD操作系统，并用其托管个人博客的实验。Wii使用IBM的PowerPC 750架构单核处理器，虽然硬件老旧，但在NetBSD的支持下，仍能处理静态网站等轻量级任务。作者首先在EMF Camp 2024活动上获得了一台Wii，并通过Wilbrand漏洞和HackMii工具安装了Homebrew Channel，进而成功运行NetBSD。文章还提到PowerPC 750芯片被广泛应用于如詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜和火星探测器等高要求任务中，强调其可靠性。最终，作者利用这台Wii搭建了一个实时状态页，展示了其性能表现。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• [Bluecobra] 对低负载平均值表示印象深刻。

This blog is hosted on a Nintendo Wii
2025-04-21 17:40
netbsd
shitpost
If you are reading this message, the experiment below is still ongoing. This page was served to you by a real Nintendo Wii.
You can check the Wii’s
live status page
for system load info.
For a long time, I’ve enjoyed the idea of running general-purpose operating systems on decidedly not-general-purpose hardware.
There’s been a few good examples of this over the years, including a few which were officially sanctioned by the OEM. Back in the day, my PS3 ran
Yellow Dog Linux
, and I’ve been searching for a (decently priced) copy of
PS2 Linux
for 10+ years at this point.
There are some other good unofficial examples, such as
Dreamcast Linux
, or
PSPLinux
.
But what a lot of these systems have in common is that they’re now very outdated. Or they’re hobbyist ports that someone got running once and where longer-term support never made it upstream. The PSP Linux kernel image was last built in 2008, and Dreamcast Linux is even more retro, using a 2.4.5 kernel built in 2001.
I haven’t seen many of these projects where I’d be comfortable running one as part of an actual production workload. Until now.
While browsing
the NetBSD website
recently, I noticed the fact that there was a ‘Wii’ option listed right there on the front page in the ‘Install Media’ section, nestled right next to the other first-class targets like the Raspberry Pi, and generic x86 machines.
Unlike the other outdated and unmaintained examples above, clicking through to the NetBSD Wii port takes you to the latest stable NetBSD 10.1 release from Dec 2024. Even the
daily HEAD builds
are composed for the Wii.
As soon as I discovered this was fully supported and maintained, I knew I had to try deploying an actual production workload on it. That workload is the blog you’re reading now.
Finding a sacrificial Wii
Our story begins at the EMF Camp 2024 Swap Shop - your premier source for pre-loved game consoles, cardboard boxes full of 56k modems, and radioactive orphan sources.
I picked this up expecting to use it for homebrew games and emulation mostly, but I don’t think it expected this fate.
Is it fast enough?
So we have a spare Wii. And an OS with mainline support. But is a Wii actually fast enough to handle this as a production workload?
The single-core ‘Broadway’ CPU in the Wii is part of IBM’s continued evolution of the PowerPC 750 lineup, dating all the way back to Apple’s iconic 1998 Bondi Blue fishtank iMac. Although Broadway is one of the later 750 revisions, the commercially-available equivalent chip - the PowerPC 750CL - has a maximum TDP of only 9.8 W, and clocks about 33% higher than the version in the Wii.
So with a single-core chip based on a late-90s architecture and a TDP well under 10 W, it’s clear that we’re probably fairly contstrained here in terms of compute performance.
With that said, one of the other PowerPC 750 deployments you might be familiar with is currently floating 1,500,000 km from Earth mapping the deepest reaches of the universe in more detail than humanity has ever seen before. So if I can’t get this thing serving a static website, then I think it’s probably time to execute on my long-term plan of retiring from tech and opening a cat cafe.
On a more serious note, you can read about the James Wii Space Telescope’s use of the PowerPC 750
in this NASA presentation
. The 750 actually gets a lot of use in spaceflight and satellite applications because there is a radiation-hardened version available, known as the
RAD750
. Some other recent uses of the chip include both the Mars
Curiosity
and
Perseverance
rovers.
Installing NetBSD on the Wii
Okay, Nintendo lawyers avert your eyes.
It had been a long time since I softmodded a Wii. I remember the
Twilight Hack
, which involved exploiting a buffer overflow in the
Twilight Princess
save game handler to run unsigned code.
Things are much easier these days. The
Wilbrand exploit
seems to be what people generally recommend now. Like some other exploits, it takes advantage of the fact that an SD card can be used to store and retrieve messages from the Wii Message Board. Exploting this allows unsigned code execution, which allows us to boot the
HackMii
tool that installs the Homebrew Channel.
It’s an easy mod which just requires knowing the MAC address of the console and generating a few files to load from an SD card. There’s a handy browser-based tool
here
which does all of the hard work for you.
I did have some issues using a larger SDHC card to run the Wilbrand exploit, but had the best luck with a 1GB non-SDHC card. SD card compatibility
seems to be a known issue
for Wii homebrew, but overall I’d still call the process fairly painless.
Once we’ve hacked the console, we should have the Homebrew Channel available in our Wii Menu:
Now we can prepare our NetBSD SD card. We do this by downloading the
wii.img.gz
image from the
front page of the NetBSD site
.
For this card, I opted to use a fairly speedy 32GB SDHC card. T

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windsurf和Cursor等AI工具的定价模式、功能表现及其对用户体验的影响

不同观点：
• **关于定价模式的批评**：
  - **amiantos** 和 **CSMastermind** 认为Windsurf和Cursor的信用额度系统不透明，导致用户难以预估实际使用成本，带来了使用焦虑。amiantos更偏好Claude Code的直接API成本，因为其成本可量化。
  - **geor9e** 和 **braza** 同样表达了对信用额度定价的不满，认为这种模式让人感到不舒服，且需要持续追踪使用情况。
  
• **关于Windsurf功能和用户体验的反馈**：
  - **SquareWheel** 分享了使用Windsurf的混合体验。虽然有时工具能有效帮助完成重复性任务，但在多数情况下，工具的自动操作错误频出，且编辑体验过于嘈杂，干扰了正常编码工作。
  - **jawns** 作为Windsurf的支持者，表示对简化定价的支持，并认为工具能有效完成其指定的任务，但对其他用户提到的体验问题未做评论。
  
• **关于Cursor和Windsurf的比较**：
  - **sunaookami** 和 **Jcampuzano2** 询问并希望了解Windsurf与Cursor在实际使用中的对比，特别是功能和性价比方面。有用户认为Windsurf的定价更低，但对其是否能在功能上与Cursor媲美存在疑问。
  
• **关于AI训练数据使用的隐私担忧**：
  - **rudedogg** 对Windsurf使用用户的输入和输出信息来训练AI表示不满，认为在用户已经付费的情况下，不应再将用户的代码数据用于产品改进。他建议使用合成数据或其他大量公开的QA数据进行训练。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现与未来发展**：
  - **cirrus3** 质疑Windsurf等工具采用自定义IDE的开发策略，认为这种做法可能不利于长期发展，并担忧未来会出现大量一次性定制IDE，而不是在现有流行IDE上开发插件或扩展。
  
• **关于定价调整的实际效果**：
  - **elashri** 提到Windsurf的定价调整让人困惑，虽然某些方案看起来更便宜，但用户需要仔细计算才能理解变化是否对自己有利。

争议焦点：
• Windsurf和Cursor的信用额度定价系统是否透明且合理。
• 用户对AI工具使用其数据进行训练的隐私担忧，以及是否应依赖合成数据或公开数据进行训练。
• Windsurf在功能上是否能真正与Cursor等工具竞争，特别是在性价比和稳定性方面。

data.title: Show HN: Open Codex – OpenAI Codex CLI with open-source LLMs
data.author: codingmoh
data.article_summary: **Open Codex**是一个开源的命令行AI助手，灵感来自OpenAI Codex，支持本地语言模型（如phi-4-mini），无需API密钥，所有操作均在本地运行。它可以将自然语言转换为shell命令，支持macOS、Linux和Windows系统。主要功能包括一次性模式、执行前确认、复制到剪贴板或直接执行等。未来计划增加交互模式、支持更多开源模型、语音输入和插件系统等。安装方式有通过Homebrew、pipx或本地克隆安装。该项目基于MIT许可证，由codingmoh开发和维护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Codex的使用、开放性及其替代方案

不同观点：
• KTibow认为无需更改，已经可以通过设置基础URL和关键环境变量来使用Codex的远程或本地API。
• xyproto表示赞赏，但指出无法与Ollama上最好的小型模型（如https://ollama.com/MFDoom/deepseek-coder-v2-tool-calling）配合使用。
• fcap质疑为何要使用开放的Codex，既然OpenAI已经为多个模型开放了该功能，试图理解其动机。
• submeta表示赞赏，但更希望Claude Code能开源，因为其在Vibe coding中表现最佳。同时提到通过API使用Anthropic的模型较贵，且存在非官方的克隆版（"Anon Kode"）。
• underlines提醒大家关注https://ollama.com/library/deepcoder，认为其在同类中排名很高。
• strangescript对默认使用Phi模型表示好奇，认为这与当前趋势不符。
• vincent0405赞赏该项目，认为这是对本地Codex替代方案的有益尝试。
• user_4028b09对Codex通过开放源代码LLM变得易于访问表示兴奋，期待尝试。
• siva7认为至少不会比使用o4-mini的原始Codex更差。
• ai-christianson质疑这并非真正的Codex，因为其完全重写了代码。
• danielktdoranie询问有关Codex Giggas的情况。
• shmoogy分享了一个链接，指出Codex今天合并了允许多个提供者的改动（https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/247）。

补充讨论：
• 对不同模型和工具的偏好和使用体验，如Ollama、Claude Code、Phi模型和deepcoder。
• 对开源和非官方版本的讨论，如Anon Kode和Codex的开放性。
• 对Codex项目本身的定义和实现方式的争议，特别是重写代码是否影响其本质。

data.title: Optimizing Heap Allocations in Go: A Case Study
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了一个因Go语言内存分配机制引发的性能问题。作者在Dolt数据库的代码 refactor 中，不小心将一个方法的接收器从指针类型改为值类型，导致系统性能下降30%。具体来说，问题的根源在于Go语言中值类型和指针类型接收器的区别。值类型接收器会引发额外的堆内存分配，从而影响性能，而指针类型接收器则不会。作者通过分析`runtime.newobject`函数的调用，找出了性能下降的原因，并通过将接收器改回指针类型解决了问题。这个案例展示了Go语言中内存分配的细节及其对性能的影响，强调了选择合适接收器类型的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Go语言中的堆栈与堆分配、逃逸分析及其在性能优化中的影响

不同观点：

data.title: Is 1 Prime, and Does It Matter?
data.author: jamespropp
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了数字1是否为质数的争议及其历史背景。古希腊数学家如毕达哥拉斯学派认为1不是数，因此不是质数，但也有如柏拉图的侄子斯普西普斯认为1是质数。历史上，欧拉和哈代等数学家也曾将1视为质数。然而，现代数学界已一致认为1不是质数。文章进一步讨论了1的独特性质，例如它是自己的倒数，并且在扩展到高斯整数等更复杂的数域中，1和-1以及i和-i具有相互为倒数的特性。最终，1被归为既非质数也非合数的特殊数。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应将1视为质数

不同观点：
• [JJMcJ] 认为1不是质数的原因是为了避免定理和证明中不断出现“不等于1”的繁琐表述。
• [wesselbindt] 从美学角度出发，认为如果1是质数，会使得算术基本定理的陈述变得冗长而不优雅。
• [scoofy] 提出数学公理是任意的，应使用最有用的公理，暗示是否将1视为质数取决于其在特定情况下的实用性。
• [cogman10] 倾向于使用“任何只有两个约数的整数”作为质数的定义，这样自然排除了1和负数。
• [jconder] 从代数数论的角度指出，如果1是质理想，会带来一些特殊性，影响数学结构的讨论。
• [alganet] 认为“只能被自身和1整除”是一个优雅的定义，并且在研究质数分布时发现不包括1的定义更方便。

补充讨论：
• [munchler] 提到了其他数学中具有争议性的问题，如0^0、0!、0/0等，指出这些问题往往选择使问题更简单的定义。
• [dullcrisp] 将1是否为质数的问题比作数组从0还是1开始的问题，并指出虽然某些定义仍可讨论，但代数数论基本解决了1是否为质数的争议。
• [pwdisswordfishz] 通过引用nLab的文章，反驳1符合欧几里得引理的观点，进一步支持1不应被视为质数。
• [pabenson] 强调1作为乘法单位元，在质数讨论中始终具有特殊性，无论其是否被包括在质数集合中。
• [ks2048] 以半开玩笑的方式建议将2也视为合数，以避免质数集中出现偶数。
• [EnPissant] 以程序员的角度，通过Python函数示例说明1不必作为质数来实现某些功能，进一步支持1不应被视为质数。

争议焦点：
• 1是否应被视为质数的主要争议在于其对数学定理和证明简洁性的影响，以及在不同数学研究背景下1的特殊性处理。

43755506.article_content:
If you ask a person on the street whether 1 is a prime number, they’ll probably pause, try to remember what they were taught, and say “no” (or “yes” or “I don’t remember”). Or maybe they’ll cross the street in a hurry. On the other hand, if you ask a mathematician, there’s a good chance they’ll say “That’s an excellent question” or “It’s kind of an interesting story…”
Some people treat the non-primeness of 1 as a mathematical fact and nothing more, but those people are missing out on something important about the nature of mathematics.
THE PREHISTORY OF PRIMES
In early days, 1 wasn’t universally regarded as a number at all. For the Pythagoreans, the first counting number was 2; 1 was the Unit from which all the numbers (2, 3, etc.) were built. So 1, not being a number, was certainly not a prime number. Euclid, although not a member of the Pythagorean Order, agreed that the first prime number was 2.
But Greek thought wasn’t homogeneous. Plato’s nephew Speussippus, for instance, thought that 1 was not only a number, but a prime number at that. So controversy about the status of 1 has a respectable pedigree.
Nor can the practice of calling 1 a prime be complacently relegated to the midden of ancient, long-discarded mistakes. The great Leonhard Euler, the pre-eminent mathematician of the eighteenth century, treated 1 as a prime in his correspondence with number-theorist Christian Goldbach. Even in the twentieth century, the mathematician G. H. Hardy, coauthor of the first great work on number theory written in the English language, classified 1 as a prime in his early writings.
Were Euler and Hardy being stupid or careless? Far from it. They were doing what good mathematicians always do: maintaining a flexible attitude toward terminology, and keeping in mind that sometimes the right way to define things only comes into focus when you’ve played with several variants.
So if your attitude toward my title was “Yeah, why
does
it matter?” you’re asking a question that Euler and Hardy – who both sometimes included 1 among the primes and sometimes didn’t – would have endorsed. After all, the number 1 has many properties in common with the primes.
1
But you shouldn’t get the idea that in the modern era there’s disagreement about the status of 1; by universal consensus, 1 isn’t a prime.
2
Does that mean we’re forced to classify 1 as a composite number, i.e., a factorable number like 4, 6, 8, and 9? Or is there a third possibility?
THE LONELIEST NUMBER
In the preface to his 1914 table of primes, the number theorist D. N. Lehmer, by way of justifying his decision to include 1 in the table, admitted that “the number 1 is certainly not composite in the same sense as the number 6,” but maintained that “if it is ruled out of the list of primes it is necessary to create a particular class for this number alone.” For Lehmer, that was sufficient reason to list 1 as a prime; leaving 1 out in the cold, calling it neither prime nor composite, didn’t seem like an option.
1 is certainly an exceptional number for many reasons. One distinctive property of the number 1 is that it’s its own reciprocal. No other positive integer has this property. When we enlarge our number system to include zero and the negative integers, 1 acquires a buddy in the person of its negative, the number −1, which, like 1, is its own reciprocal. Further enlarging our scope to include the rational numbers and the real numbers brings us no new numbers with this property. But when we enlarge yet again, to the complex numbers, although we don’t get any new numbers that are their own reciprocals, we get two numbers that are simultaneously each other’s negatives
and
each other’s reciprocals:
i
and −
i
.
Just as the integers form an interesting subsystem of the real numbers, the
Gaussian integers
— complex numbers of the form
a
+
bi
where
a
and
b
are ordinary integers — form an interesting subsystem of the complex numbers. The Gaussian integers taken in aggregate form what mathematicians call an
integral domain
(in this essay I’ll use the shorter term “domain” for brevity) in which numbers can safely be added, subtracted, or multiplied without ever leaving the domain. Notice that I left division off the list of safe operations; in a domain, you usually can’t divide one element by another. But when a special element of a domain — call it
u
— has the property that the reciprocal of
u
also belongs to that domain, then
every
element of the domain can be divided by
u
: just multiply that element by the reciprocal of
u
. In the domain of integers, the only such elements are
u
= 1 and
u
= −1, but in the domain of Gaussian integers, there are four of them: 1, −1,
i
and −
i
.
An even more interesting example is the domain consisting of all numbers of the form
a
+
b
sqrt(2) where again
a
and
b
are ordinary integers. In this domain there are
infinitely
many numbers whose reciprocals belong to that same domain: for instance, 1 + sqrt(2) and −1 + sqrt(2) are each other’s reciproca

data.title: Dumb statistical models, always making people look bad
data.author: hackandthink
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：统计模型与人类判断的比较，尤其是在预测和决策中的表现和价值。

不同观点：
• **统计模型优于人类判断**：[vintermann]、[gwern]和[delichon]认为，统计模型在聚合数据和做出预测方面通常优于人类，尤其是在处理大量相似数据时。他们指出，模型通过减少聚合损失来优化预测，并且在许多情况下，模型可以超越人类的专业判断，甚至通过引导模型开发来利用人类知识，但最终模型的表现更优。[gwern]特别提到，即使是复杂的AI系统也能通过减少人类随机错误而表现得更好。

• **人类在特殊情况下更优**：[rawgabbit]、[dominicq]和[reedf1]认为，人类在处理新颖情况、数据稀缺或需要判断数据是否错误时表现更好。例如，人类能够识别假数据或在数据不充分的情况下做出判断，而模型可能无法处理这些情况。[dominicq]指出，专业人员应专注于模型难以处理的罕见事件或数据不足的领域。[reedf1]进一步强调，人类可以扩展其内部模型的自由度，整合样本外数据，并在个体层面做出更具人性偏差的决策。

• **统计模型的局限性**：[3abiton]和[bicepjai]指出，统计模型虽然有用，但并非万能。他们提到在实际工作中，统计数据常常被低估，非技术利益相关者更倾向于使用轶事证据而非统计数据进行决策。此外，[bicepjai]引用“所有模型都是愚蠢的，但有些是有用的”来强调模型的局限性。

• **模型解释性和错误处理**：[reedf1]和[whatever1]关注模型的解释性和错误处理能力。他们认为，如果模型无法提供人类可解释的预测理由，那么其改进可能只是过拟合。此外，[whatever1]指出，统计模型可能在所有使用的情况下都出错，而人类在犯错时能承担责任，这在某些情况下可能比平均正确性更重要。

补充讨论：
• **工具使用和人类判断**：[nitwit005]提到，人类是工具使用者，统计表等工具是人类判断的辅助手段，并不一定取代人类判断。

• **案例分析**：[rawgabbit]通过Frank案例分析了人类专家如何识别假数据，强调了人类经验在识别数据异常中的价值。

争议焦点：统计模型在聚合数据上的优越性与人类在特殊情况和解释性上的优势之间的平衡与取舍。

data.title: Local LLM inference – impressive but too hard to work with
data.author: aazo11
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了本地运行大语言模型（LLM）推理的潜力和挑战。作者在开发文本到SQL产品的过程中，研究了是否能将生成型BI堆栈集成到浏览器中，从而深入探索了本地推理。尽管通过开源软件，普通笔记本电脑现在可以在浏览器中免费运行强大的LLM，但本地推理尚未完全准备好作为开发者平台用于生产环境。

本地计算的优势包括成本低、隐私保护、速度快和支持离线使用。虽然iPhone面部解锁等应用已经证明了本地推理的可行性，但在软件开发中广泛采用仍面临模型选择和部署的困难。当前的本地推理框架如llama.cpp、Ollama和WebLLM在性能上各有优劣，但均不及云端解决方案。此外，小型模型的下载和加载时间较长，影响了用户体验。

作者认为，本地LLM推理技术已具备一定基础，但开发工具尚需成熟，才能在实际应用中广泛使用。未来需要简化模型训练和部署，并实现与云端LLM的无缝集成。

• [Havoc] 不同意成本观点，认为API成本低于本地GPU运行成本，且有许多免费令牌可用。
• [segmondy] 强调本地LLM的优势在于可以找到许多没有云对应的模型，并根据特定需求进行微调。
• [ranger_danger] 提到llamafile可能是解决本地运行困难的方案，并提供了一个GitHub链接作为参考。
• [aazo11] 通过个人项目经验指出，尽管可以在普通笔记本上运行LLM，但找到特定任务模型和处理大模型下载是主要挑战。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是本地运行LLM的成本与效率对比云服务的优劣。
• 另一个焦点是技术门槛，包括硬件要求、模型选择和下载成本对用户体验的影响。
• 不同硬件（如Mac的统一内存架构）和技术工具（如Ollama、LM Studio、llamafile）的优劣也被广泛讨论。

43753890.article_content:
Local LLM inference
Amir Zohrenejad
·
Follow
4 min read
·
4 hours ago
--
Listen
Share
Tremendous progress, but not ready for production
I stumbled into local inference during a side quest. The main mission was to build a text-to-SQL product. Curiosity hijacked the roadmap: could I cram an entire GenBI stack into the browser?
The prototype never shipped. But I did fall into the local inference rabbit hole. Though “AI inference” is not a listed feature on my laptop spec sheet — through the magic of open source software it can now run powerful LLMs in its browser tabs for free. It’s impressive. Just not
quite
production-ready as a developer platform.
Why bother with local compute?
From mainframes to PCs to the cloud, compute has swung between centralization and edge. Now it’s drifting back
toward the edge
— at least if you squint through the hype. But most users don’t actually care
where
computation happens. They want it to be fast, and they want it to be cheap.
For example: Figma isn’t popular because it runs on WebAssembly — users love it because it feels instant. DuckDB isn’t getting traction in the data world because it fits on a laptop — it’s being deployed because it can trim Snowflake bills.
Most applications still run in the cloud. However there are four benefits to moving compute to the local device:
Cost
Privacy
Speed
Enabling offline use
Local inference is not new:
iPhone facial unlock
has implemented local inference on mobile devices at scale since 2018. Facial unlock wouldn’t work without local inference: it has to be fast, work offline, be private and not cost Apple money every time someone tries to unlock their phone.
As software applications increasingly integrate LLMs, pushing AI inference to the edge can have the same upside.
Frameworks
I tested the following local inference frameworks together with quantized versions of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B.
llama.cpp
: C/C++ core, highly optimized. An amazing project by
Georgi Gerganov
.
Ollama
: A product and business built on llama.cpp. Better DevEx and model library curation.
WebLLM
: Browser-based inference with WebGPU acceleration developed at Carnegie Mellon. Built on
MLC
.
I ran the inference benchmarks against OpenAI’s
gpt-4.0-mini
as a baseline comparison. The benchmark code can be found
here
.
Performance
Tests were run on my Macbook Pro with the following chip specs, with 32GB of RAM.
The metrics I tracked were median
time to first token (TTFT)
and
tokens per second (TPS)
.
As the chart above shows, llama.cpp and Ollama are both blazing fast in TTFT. OpenAI is slightly slower, likely due to network overhead and authentication. WebLLM was the slowest.
In terms of TPS, llama.cpp and ollama are comparable, which makes sense as they are the same under the hood. WebLLM topped out at only half of the TPS of the other frameworks. I can only assume this is because WebGPU acceleration is not as efficient in utilizing local GPU as the llama.cpp implementation that accesses the GPU directly.
All the local inference solutions were slower than OpenAI running
gpt-4.0-mini
, a considerably larger model.
While I did not track memory usage or CPU/GPU utilization, I did not notice any noticeable side effects while using other apps on my laptop as the benchmarks ran.
Mo’ Models, Mo’ Problems
While the performance of local inference lags cloud solutions, it is already good enough for many tasks. This brings us to the main problem I encountered: finding and deploying the correct model for a given task.
Given the resource constraints, the models that run locally must be much smaller than models running on the cloud. For a developer, there is currently no way to find (or easily tune) a model that can do “text-to-SQL” and work on a Macbook with M2 chip. Even when I had shelved the prototype idea and was just aiming to benchmark these tools with deepseek-qwen-7B, I had to decide which of the 663 different models that match this name on HuggingFace I should download for llama.cpp.
Furthermore, even a quantized version of a distilled 7B model is over 5GB. Downloading and loading these models is very slow even on fiber internet. For an application developer, this leads to a degraded initial user experience of the application. For example, if your webapp uses WebLLM, the user will need to sit for a few
minutes
while the model is being downloaded to their machine.
Final thoughts
Local LLM inference is possible. It works today, but the developer tooling will need to mature before real world applications leverage local inference beyond niche use cases.
Any real solution will need to make it dead simple to train and deploy small, task-specific models — and integrate tightly with cloud LLMs. It will have to handle downloads, caching, and local execution behind the scenes, so the user never notices where the model is running or how it got there.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple设备和iCloud账户在被盗后的安全问题及账户恢复流程的争议

不同观点：
• crazygringo认为，Apple应该建立一个验证流程（如电话号码、信用卡、购买收据等）来帮助用户恢复账户，尤其是用户在Apple设备上花费了大量金钱，账户恢复是合理且必要的。他质疑是否因为法律责任问题，Apple不愿意介入账户恢复。

• nashashmi分享了一个实例，其亲戚的手机被盗后，小偷成功更改了iCloud账户的密码和邮箱，导致家人无法重置手机。这表明当前的账户安全措施存在漏洞，容易被不法分子利用。

• someonehere不信任Apple的账户安全机制，建议用户自行备份数据，并提供了两种备份方案（Backblaze云备份或本地硬盘备份）。他强调依赖Apple的风险性。

• gu009指出，在手机被盗后如何处理缺乏明确指导，Apple的官方建议没有涵盖实际盗窃中窃贼使用的社会工程手段。他建议Apple应区分“丢失”和“被盗”的情况，并提供更多针对性的保护措施。

• alabastervlog推测问题可能出在iCloud账户的“忘记密码”功能上，如果手机上保存了相关邮箱账户，小偷可以轻易获取iCloud账户的访问权限。

• mmmlinux持批评态度，认为很多问题是用户自己没有保管好终极恢复密码，而不是Apple的责任。

• anonym29以讽刺的语气批评了对大公司和政府的信任，认为用户不应盲目依赖Apple等大公司，建议考虑自托管、开源系统等替代方案。

• JCattheATM对消费者表示有限同情，认为将数字生活托管给大公司（如Apple）是有风险的，因为这些公司往往不关心个体用户。

• tacker2000认为Apple不应该介入账户恢复，尤其是在用户没有本地备份的情况下，数据丢失的责任应由用户自己承担。他质疑如果Apple开放恢复流程，如何在更大范围内有效执行。

• betimsl为Apple的加密机制辩护，指出Apple的端到端加密设计初衷是保护用户隐私，Apple自身无法解密数据，即使有传票要求也是如此。他认为Apple在隐私和安全之间选择了隐私。

补充讨论：
- 用户对Apple在账户安全和恢复方面的期望与Apple自身政策之间的矛盾。
- 对大公司（如Apple）的信任问题，部分用户认为不应完全依赖大公司。
- 具体案例（如nashashmi的亲身经历）揭示了当前系统中的安全漏洞。
- 对如何有效应对手机被盗后的账户安全问题提出了具体建议（如gu009的“标记为被盗”选项）。
- 账户恢复技术实现的可行性问题，包括如何在更大范围内操作以及数据隐私的保护。

• crazygringo认为，Apple应该建立一个验证流程（如电话号码、信用卡、购买收据等）来帮助用户恢复账户，尤其是用户在Apple设备上花费了大量金钱，账户恢复是合理且必要的。他质疑是否因为法律责任问题，Apple不愿意介入账户恢复。

• nashashmi分享了一个实例，其亲戚的手机被盗后，小偷成功更改了iCloud账户的密码和邮箱，导致家人无法重置手机。这表明当前的账户安全措施存在漏洞，容易被不法分子利用。

• someonehere不信任Apple的账户安全机制，建议用户自行备份数据，并提供了两种备份方案（Backblaze云备份或本地硬盘备份）。他强调依赖Apple的风险性。

• gu009指出，在手机被盗后如何处理缺乏明确指导，Apple的官方建议没有涵盖实际盗窃中窃贼使用的社会工程手段。他建议Apple应区分“丢失”和“被盗”的情况，并提供更多针对性的保护措施。

• alabastervlog推测问题可能出在iCloud账户的“忘记密码”功能上，如果手机上保存了相关邮箱账户，小偷可以轻易获取iCloud账户的访问权限。

• mmmlinux持批评态度，认为很多问题是用户自己没有保管好终极恢复密码，而不是Apple的责任。

• anonym29以讽刺的语气批评了对大公司和政府的信任，认为用户不应盲目依赖Apple等大公司，建议考虑自托管、开源系统等替代方案。

• JCattheATM对消费者表示有限同情，认为将数字生活托管给大公司（如Apple）是有风险的，因为这些公司往往不关心个体用户。

• tacker2000认为Apple不应该介入账户恢复，尤其是在用户没有本地备份的情况下，数据丢失的责任应由用户自己承担。他质疑如果Apple开放恢复流程，如何在更大范围内有效执行。

• betimsl为Apple的加密机制辩护，指出Apple的端到端加密设计初衷是保护用户隐私，Apple自身无法解密数据，即使有传票要求也是如此。他认为Apple在隐私和安全之间选择了隐私。

补充讨论：
- 用户对Apple在账户安全和恢复方面的期望与Apple自身政策之间的矛盾。
- 对大公司（如Apple）的信任问题，部分用户认为不应完全依赖大公司。
- 具体案例（如nashashmi的亲身经历）揭示了当前系统中的安全漏洞。
- 对如何有效应对手机被盗后的账户安全问题提出了具体建议（如gu009的“标记为被盗”选项）。

data.title: Lichens can survive almost anything, and some might survive Mars
data.author: abacussh
data.article_summary: 文章主要探讨了地衣是否能在火星恶劣环境下生存。研究人员在模拟火星环境的条件下，测试了两种地衣（*Diploschistes muscorum*和*Cetrarea aculeata*）的生存能力。结果显示，这些地衣在低压、低温、高二氧化碳和强辐射的环境中，仍能保持一定的代谢活性。虽然两种地衣都表现出耐辐射能力，但*D. muscorum*比*C. aculeata*更具抗性，且其光合作用未受显著影响。研究表明，地衣可能具有在火星上生存的潜力，但具体生存能力取决于物种及其适应性。研究人员认为还需进一步研究以确认地衣能否真正适应火星环境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于文章未提及Kim Stanley Robinson的《火星三部曲》的评论，以及对火星相关科幻作品的不同看法。

不同观点：
• [NoTeslaThrow] 认为文章遗漏了《火星三部曲》是严重的缺失，并对该作品给予高度评价。他认为这部作品是极少数同时具备硬科幻特性和乐观、生动角色描绘的佳作，值得读者关注。同时提到Ursula K. Le Guin的《一无所有》作为类似作品。
• [elevatedastalt] 以幽默的方式回应，提到自己误将"lichen"（地衣）看成"Lichess"（一个国际象棋网站），并以此表示对原评论的认同。
• [morkalork] 提出一个假设情景，即如果探测器污染导致地衣在火星上扩散，可能会产生尴尬后果。这种观点引入了对太空探测中生物污染问题的潜在担忧。
• [djaouen] 以简短幽默的方式评论，暗示与人类相比，地衣可能更适合或更有趣地存在于火星上。
• [contingencies] 用双关语"Mars: I'm lichen it"表达了对地衣和火星主题的兴趣，与之前的评论形成互动。

• 评论中对《火星三部曲》的高度赞扬，尤其是其对地衣等自然元素的详尽描述，反映了部分读者对硬科幻作品中科学细节和世界构建的重视。
